  • It has been revealed that if you didn't already know, Dave The Diver actually has something in common with Rockstar's new open-world title, Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Well, before we get too carried away, GTA 6 might already be on the mind of the Dave the Diver developer Mintrocket, as the game's official social media account has shared a rather amusing image today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you didn't already know, Dave The Diver actually has something in common with Rockstar's new open-world title, Grand Theft Auto 6. In both games, you can go diving!

Now, can you imagine a collab? Well, before we get too carried away, GTA 6 might already be on the mind of the Dave the Diver developer Mintrocket, as the game's official social media account has shared a rather amusing image today. Here it is:.

If you've been playing GTA 6 over the past week, this character may look familiar, as it appears to be Mintrocket's nod to an individual known as Brian (not to be mistaken with the Dave the Diver character, Cobra). The male protagonist in GTA 6 (Jason) works for Brian.

The whole look, including the shirt, seems very similar to Rockstar's character. And then there's the Vice City-like backdrop. Just about every reply to the post so far seems to be open to the idea of Brian coming to Blue Hole in some way or form. However, as one fan notes, it might be hard to get him out of retirement.

According to recent reports, while there's no guarantee anything will come of this, it's worth noting Dave the Diver has already done some crazy (and high-profile) crossovers with titles and series such as Yakuza: Like A Dragon and Godzilla. Dave has also appeared in games such as Epic's battle royale, Fortnite.

As part of the GTA 6 marketing campaign, Rockstar did a collab with NBA 2K27, another title under parent company Take-Two.

A lot of developers have been plugging their own games and series with all sorts of GTA-inspired advertising and jokes over the past week, but if this does lead to something more than this, we'll let you know.

All the GTA 6 stat boost missions we've found

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that missions that permanently boost max Health, Stamina, and Focus in GTA 6 appear in a few places.
  • Recent findings suggest that as well as being worth seeking them out if you want to buff your stats, they also include some of the best and weirdest missions in the game, so it's a double win if you do go after them.
  • The map above reveals where you you start each mission.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that missions that permanently boost max Health, Stamina, and Focus in GTA 6 appear in a few places. However, you'll never know there's a buff until you complete them and all but one are hidden away, meaning you'll need to find them by chance or get lucky.

Recent findings suggest that as well as being worth seeking them out if you want to buff your stats, they also include some of the best and weirdest missions in the game, so it's a double win if you do go after them. I've not included the meditation spots in GTA 6 that also boost your max Focus here, as that's a whole thing in it's own right.

The map above reveals where you you start each mission. Some are single hit jobs where you do one thing and get the boost, others require a few steps and you might have to wait to continue.

According to recent reports, I've covered the whole GTA 6 aliens thing fully already, but the short version is you need to be abducted (the map shows where it happened for me), by looking out for an abandoned car at night with all its light flashing. After that you need to sleep, where a dream will show you the rest of the way. Read my full guide for all the details but completing this will permanently increase your Health, Stamina, and Focus.

The GTA 6 Final Flush mission can be started by scanning the QR code you find in the bathroom marked above. It's at Corsair Key, near where you start the game. Once you've done that you'll get a second marker to meet someone at a waffle house. Read our guide for the full walkthrough, but at the end of it you'll come out with a permanent increase in max Stamina.

This is the only mission that's pointed out to you when you scan the crop dusting poster outside the motel reception in chapter 2. This will direct you to McKittrick Farm marked on the map above. You'll need to dust the crops first but that will then lead to a mission later where you need to get some chemicals. Complete that and you'll have the chance to eat a mutated strawberry that will permanently increase your max Stamina. You'll get a text later to close out this mission and, while there are no more stat boosts, I highly recommend seeing how it all ends.

The Circles of Hell mission sees you visit Satan and blow him away Doom style. You'll need to find the garage marked above in Port Gellhorn somewhere around midnight. You'll know it's the right time because it'll be open and lit up red. Talk to the people inside and go with them to meet the dark lord and kill him. If you fail at all at this point, check the wooden throne for some more 'shrooms so you can try again. Defeat the hordes and you'll get a permanent increase to your max Health, plus a shotgun and t-shirt.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Industry observers note that if you head all the way out to Lake Tallaloko north of Milliport you'll find a logging yard full of felled trees. Make your way to the location on the map and you'll find a yellow shipping crate you can enter. At least one person here at GR reported needing the cut-off tool in GTA 6 to open it, but when I found it (before having the tool) it was just open. Inside you'll find a mysterious psychedelic box you can interact with. Do that and you'll have to complete a trippy obstacle course made of crates and logs. Get through it and you'll get a permanent max Stamina increase and fresh tattoo.

Industry observers note that head roughly to this area on the map (near where you can get abducted by aliens at night) and listen out for shouting and gunfire in the woods, near the road construction site. Here you’ll find a group of self-proclaimed ‘ecologists’ doing some environmental hunting of invasive species. Pick up the Duke 556 Assault Rifle on the barrel to begin the ‘practice round’ shooting static targets such as pumpkins, and then you’ll be prompted to wager $250 on the main challenge - shooting a bunch of iguanas released from a cage. Win and you'll get $250 plus a max Focus increase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yep, he's back. Less than two weeks after Jensen Huang resigned from being CEO of Nvidia following reports of multiple affairs, the company's board have reinstated him "effective immediately".

"The board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candour and ability to lead Nvidia," the organization revealed. "In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

In a recent development, "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," added recently appointed chairman Harvey Jones, who'll remain in the post following Huang's return. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's short break, will go back to just being chief financial officer.

Sources indicate that "I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang declared. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.".

Recent findings suggest that oh, and Nvidia's board added that the independent investigation they set in motion "in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort" will "proceed to conclusion". Huang "fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it", they noted.

Sources indicate that since resigning amid the scandal, Huang had made it clear he'd be open to returning to his post if the Nvidia board okayed it and had several powerful people either call for his reinstatement or declare they'd consider hiring him. "The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy," one such advocate, US president Donald Trump, has reportedly posted to cursed hellcape Truth social. Huang is a "great patriot and national treasure", the Trumpeter added.

Industry observers note that so, there you go. I'm not saying that you're totally immune to consequences for alleged actions that'd lose any normal person their job for far more than 11 days if you're mates with the American president, but it sure does look like that, doesn't it? Hope Nvidia didn't throw out any leather jackets Huang couldn't manage to carry out of the building with him.

Industry News: After taking seven years to make Persona 6 and four years to make Persona 5, Atlus promises future games will come quicker

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (384 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.
  • Sources indicate that there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped.
  • P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

Sources indicate that there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day.".

It has been revealed that wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus intends to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

In a recent development, we don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Playtonic has announced Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair is being treated to a upcoming Definitive Edition on PS5, and it's right around the corner.

The upcoming version releases on 15th December 2026, and anyone who owns a digital PS4 version of the game gets a free upgrade. It appears anyone with a physical copy won't get the upgrade.

Industry observers note that on base PS5 and PS5 Pro, the latest edition will support a 4K resolution at 120fps, better lighting and ambient occlusion effects, higher-fidelity shadows, and two orchestrated soundtracks. Also, if you don't already own it, the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack is automatically bundled in with the PS5 version.

Sources indicate that one of the best platforming adventures of its generation is back, enhanced for PlayStation 5. Yooka & Laylee return for a full-scale 2.5D adventure, with a 3D Overworld that's an adventure in its own right, levels you can alter to create latest ways to play, and Capital B's Impossible Lair waiting to test your skills.

Sources indicate that A 2D and top-down side game that accompanies the main Yooka-Laylee game, the Impossible Lair went down really well upon its original launch. It's got an 82 rating on Metacritic, and in our own review, we called it an "improvement" on the original adventure.

We've got quite a few interesting Xbox releases still to come in December, and one of them that we've been keeping a close eye on is Stage Tour, which is a newly introduced Guitar Hero / Rock Band style game launching on December 10th.

In a recent development, they're not messing around with this one either, having snagged loads of famous bands for the tracklist, which now stands at well over 70 songs. There are going to be 90+ by the time we get to release, so there's more to come.

Let's take a look at all the confirmed songs so far:.

Stage Tour is right now available to pre-order on the Xbox Store at a price of £31.49 / $35.99 (with Xbox Play Anywhere support included), but obviously that assumes you already have an instrument to play the game with, such as the Riffmaster that we reviewed last year.

Recent findings suggest that you'll also find hardware being sold alongside the game at various retailers, with the game and guitar bundle retailing at £119.99 here in the UK. There's also a drum kit, and band kit, and much more on the official Stage Tour website.

I'm personally just planning to stick with the Riffmaster and see whether Stage Tour can do enough to hold my attention amidst the likes of Rock Band 4, Clone Hero and YARG across console and PC, and I'm particularly intrigued by the "all-new roguelite Tour Mode" that apparently makes for an endlessly replayable campaign.

  • Recent findings suggest that fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players, which isn't bad for a game that's at the moment only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

It has been revealed that alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active consumers drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.

Recent findings suggest that fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend. EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 released," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M.".

According to recent reports, but where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott indicates: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

According to recent reports, during that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.

As Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable.".

Breaking: GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.
  • Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November.
  • As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a newly introduced record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a newly introduced record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

Sources indicate that for context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

Industry observers note that "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a fresh chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," mentioned Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.".

In a recent development, previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent tech giant Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

According to recent reports, "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#223814. Feature: Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1187 w)

Feature: Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score.
  • Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur.
  • Industry observers note that we've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score. But just because we gave it a 10/10 here at Pure Xbox doesn't mean there isn't still some wiggle room for improvement.

Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur. However, we've also noticed a few things we'd like to see fixed or added to GTA VI to make it even better. Think of this article like adding marshmallows to a hot chocolate: we're looking to take something great and make it even sweeter.

Industry observers note that we've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI. Let's get into it:.

Industry observers note that you've all noticed the darkness that appears from time to time around the screen, right? That's a vignette and GTA VI is a big fan of them. It's most noticeable when you're booking it down the North 97 highway or, in the worst-case scenario, flying over the Keys as shown in the above screenshot.

GTA VI uses vignettes to cleverly draw your focus to the most vital parts of the screen. I honestly think it's a great technique for making things feel more cinematic. Although, it is quite pants that there's no option to reduce its intensity or turn it off altogether. If Rockstar could give us the ability to toggle the vignette on and off, that would be great, because it also seems to be one of the most requested changes amongst GTA VI players.

Industry observers note that something I've grown increasingly aware of is the inability to wait or sleep to pass time across Leonida. I was particularly irked after an 18-hole crazy golf competition against Jason saw the sun set on us, and I didn't fancy driving all the way back to my lodging in Vice City. I wanted to pass time in my car or a nearby eatery, but my only option appeared to be the 4-5 minute drive home - made worse knowing that once morning hit, I'd just want to do the drive back and play golf in the daylight.

Industry observers note that it's probably the fault of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its extremely handy wilderness camps. They were great in a pinch to let you pass time quickly. What would be great is if GTA VI gave players the option to rough it in their car for the night or find a nearby hotel room or something.

In a recent development, I was on a mission to pick up some prescription drugs when my car was escorted slowly into an enemy compound and the camera suddenly switched from third-person to first-person. Seeing Lucia's impeccable nails gripped around the steering wheel made me realise there's no legitimate way to drive from a behind-the-wheel perspective.

Sure, there's that glitch that lets you play GTA VI in first-person, but it would be better if Rockstar implemented an additional first-person POV for driving.

It seems like a bit of a no-brainer, but we'd love to see AMD FSR 4.1 implementation on Xbox Series X. GTA VI is already up-and-running with FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S which brings internal resolutions up from 720p to 1080p output. It's good going on XSS, but we'd like to see what it can do with XSX.

In a recent development, if a game introduces with a good Photo Mode, then you may as well tack an extra 10 hours onto my playthrough. But GTA VI? Maybe add another 20-30 hours. It's gorgeous!

It has been revealed that the Photo Mode in this game is already solid. You can set up light sources, adjust focus and aperture, and as a graduate photographer, I think it's all rather intuitive. There's even a selfie mode where players can pose Jason and Lucia together, adjust their facial expressions and change their poses.

What I'd like to see is that same flexibility expand beyond selfie mode. I'd like to be able to adjust the lovers to better match the photos I'm trying to create. It was during a tense getaway, four-stars and neck-deep in trouble, that I thought I'd take an action shot, only to find Jason had blinked and Lucia looked bored as hell. It would be great to have the option to adjust expressions, head directions, poses and all that sort of stuff.

Recent findings suggest that please fix the sliders when handling amounts of money, Rockstar. Please. It's not the biggest fix, nor the most elaborate, so I'll keep it brief.

Whenever I open my phone to buck myself some cash, I often struggle to select the right amount swiftly. It takes too long for the slider to speed up as I increase the amount, but then it very quickly gets out of control, and I end up overshooting my intended figure. Plus, the sound it makes is quite horrid.

What would help is having set increments to scroll through, say, $1, $10, $50, $100 and so on. It might just smooth out the experience a smidge.

I'd like to wrap up with a quickfire segment of some of our own suggestions on how Rockstar could improve GTA VI, but also some of yours. So, let's get through it.

It has been revealed that I'd love to be able to call NPC buddies like Cal for a round of crazy golf. At the moment, playing with a partner is limited to Jason and Lucia. I'm all for love, but sometimes you need some friendly bonding too.

Recent findings suggest that another one I'd personally like to see is custom music stations on in-game radios. Now, I know this isn't something likely to happen, but it would be cool to link my Spotify and Rockstar accounts to play my own curated playlists.

It has been revealed that oh, and for the love of all things matrimony, please let me make a coffee for Jason/Lucia and actually give it to them. I've experienced Jason asking for a cuppa joe, so let me do the do, y'know?

It has been revealed that something Fraser mentioned he'd like to see is additional minigames like bowling or darts added to the game. The developers stated they ran out of time for things like this, so maybe they could add them as a post-launch update.

And to wrap up, I've spotted folks online requesting the ability to dial any phone number like you could in previous games, as well as blind firing around cover during firefights, buying housing property, and having save states pick up directly where you left off.

So, there you have it. Some of our suggestions and some we've found out in the wild, but we'd love to hear your ideas on what might make GTA VI a better game. Be sure to chat with us in the comments!

GTA 6's best lore drops happen when you're chilling with your partner, so stop leaving them at home all the time

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that my real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk.
  • Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that my real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do.

And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments.

Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful.

But then, occasionally, beyond all the comedic conversations and flavour dialogue that give these characters so much life, the game'll drop some proper good lore. I'll do my best not to spoil stuff here, but for almost every complaint I've seen on social media about why certain protagonists did certain things, there's an answer tucked away in these interactions. The kind of things you'd really want to know about these characters? Your best chance of finding it all out is when you bring them together.

Industry observers note that I've really enjoyed having lore drops unfold in mundane conversations while walking around, driving, or eating a burger, rather than hamfisted into the main story. They feel like natural breathing moments for the couple to recount the past, or get into the stuff that was happening in the time that they were apart. You know, the exact kind of times actual couples and friends would find the time to dig into these things in real life, too.

It has been revealed that that doesn't mean you have to keep them together all the time. Some of their exclusive missions also provide a great bit of insight into their backstories—like Jason's side stuff with ex-army pal Bret Vogel, or the missions that have Lucia in some all-too-real situations with her mother.

I've played plenty of the game flying solo as both protagonists too, and you'll occasionally get some of this nattering just by hanging around in your abode together. But I can't recommend enough that you find plenty of opportunities to bring them together out in the open world. Even if it's just for 15 minutes here and there, you'll uncover a whole lot about who they were before we first got to know them as the player. And as someone who has really enjoyed learning just about everything about these two as I can, it's been one of my favourite parts of the game so far.

  • "Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".

In a recent development, "I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling).

It has been revealed that the role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also claims steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character.".

A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

"That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he stated, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made.".

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

Sources indicate that "Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose said there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

It has been revealed that rose also notes many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!".

Finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are currently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union.".

GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It launched on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Netflix's The Body was one of the unexpected hits of the 2026 TV schedule. While it's still yet to be confirmed whether we'll get to stream a second season with a Netflix subscription, it feels like the odds are looking good. So I'm glad the executive producers/showrunners are already shooting down some fan theories before any fresh episodes come out.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, creator Quinn Shephard and co-showrunner Gina Gammell didn't tell Glamour all the biggest secrets surrounding Grace and whether this is truly spiritual or classic Catholic School drama, Luckily, though, fans did learn a couple of key details. I'm happy about both of these theories being addressed, especially the one that sounds like good news for Leo.

If you're a fan of Leo and think he's too pure for this world, Quinn Shepard confirming he did not bring a snake to the Halloween party should bring you some comfort. It's been theorized that Leo brought his pet snake to the party, perhaps in an attempt to heal Grace. This was supported by the fact that Leo and Grace came from a cult called Signs Following, which used snake handling as a means of showing the faith of its followers.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, Leo seemed concerned about other characters outside of his family seeing the snake during the investigation into Grace's coma. With this context, it's possible that Leo was just concerned about hiding their true religious beliefs, as they lied about being Catholics to get rehomed after leaving West Virginia.

In a recent development, I'm so glad the EPs have also confirmed the Lions won't be going to jail after what happened to Grace. I thought that was a possibility, given Anya's confession and the various details about the party that came out toward the end of Season 1.

I Just Watched The Trailer For Netflix's JonBenèt Ramsey Drama, And I Feel A Bit Uneasy.

It has been revealed that while I'm all for accountability in teen dramas, especially when it comes to Riverdale's Archie Andrews, I'll let it slide for The Body. Sending Anya or any of the Lions to jail or prison for their actions at the party would've created a major genre shift in the story, and I'm far more interested in the story remaining around the school after Season 1's ending.

Sources indicate that of course, we still have to wait for official word on Season 2 of The Body. While I think Netflix should be bullish on a renewal given the talented young cast and the fact it's been on Netflix's Top 10 charts in recent weeks, there's really no telling what the streamer will decide to do with the series. It's a well known fact that the firm has canceled plenty of shows way too soon, so we best just cross our fingers and hope a Grace-sized miracle grants the series a renewal soon.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's vital questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

According to recent reports, in this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

It has been revealed that you can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

Sources indicate that the cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Sources indicate that would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

It's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Marsden claims his comic-accurate Cyclops suit in Avengers: Doomsday gives the audience “everything that they want to see" – even if the actor might not be feeling so snug after stepping out of the black leather.

“The comic-accurate suit was very exciting for me to do, but [they] still haven’t figured out the comfort thing yet,” Marsden told Entertainment Weekly of his brightly colored ensemble piece, which largely mirrors the X-Men leader's traditional wear.

It has been revealed that “No, it was great. It was one of those pinch-me moments where you’re playing this iconic character and then coming back and giving the fans everything that they want to see.”.

Famously, the original X-Men trilogy cracked a joke at the expense of the superhero group's colorful array of costumes. When Hugh Jackman's Wolverine grumbled about the black leather in 2000's X-Men, Cyclops deadpanned if he would prefer "yellow spandex" instead.

It has been revealed that in recent years, Marvel Studios has given the X-Men its due on the costume front. Deadpool and Wolverine not only featured Logan in his traditional yellow and blue outfit, but also dealt Gambit a winning hand with his comic book-style suit.

With Disney's acquisition of Fox, Kevin Feige – who had a behind-the-scenes production role on the first X-Men – is finally able to make his cinematic universe dreams come true, with even Marsden admitting there had been "so much chatter" in the past about bringing the mutant team to the MCU.

Recent findings suggest that so, costume? Check. A fully-fledged role instead of nostalgia bait? Check. A leading light in the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, complete with iconic catchphrase? Check, check, and check. If you're a Cyclops fan, you'll be eating well this holiday season.

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

Recent findings suggest that while critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take glitch with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

In a recent development, "Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and latest features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality.".

"Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

In a recent development, "The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****.".

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

Industry observers note that "A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close.".

Guide: GTA 6: Secret Controls the Game Doesn't Tell You

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (846 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has a complicated control scheme that allows you to interact with the game in a variety of different ways.
  • Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.
  • Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has a complicated control scheme that allows you to interact with the game in a variety of different ways. And while Rockstar does a good job introducing almost all of the title's mechanics, several useful features and commands are never mentioned at all. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you about some of its secret controls.

Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.

Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.

Double tap Triangle to get out of your car while the engine's still running:.

This can be useful for when you need to make a swift getaway, as you want waste time needing to start the engine.

One other quick tip here: if you're with a partner and need to promptly get into the back seat, hold Triangle so your character doesn't waste time running around to the passenger side.

If the police know your identity but not necessarily your car, one way you can avoid being detected is by hiding behind the wheel.

Just park up somewhere discreet, and hold Circle to hide from any pursuing police:.

You can rest and lean on any surface by standing close to it and holding the Circle button, like shown:.

This can be useful if you're casing a joint, or just want to watch the world pass you by.

You don't always need words to get your point across. There are situations where a middle finger will do.

Fortunately, GTA 6 has a solution for scenarios just like that.

While on foot, hold L2 and press R1 to give someone the finger:.

You can also do this while driving by simply pressing R1 while behind the wheel:.

Tapping Left and Right while driving will turn on your indicators, allowing you to signal to other motorists which way you're going:.

Industry observers note that this can actually be useful when you're trying to drive safely, as oncoming cars will understand which way you're going and react accordingly. It can also help when you're merging lanes on motorways.

While more complex radio controls can be accessed by holding Left, did you know you can also quickly turn the radio on and off by double-tapping Left?

This works both in a car and when you're out and about using your earbuds.

If you press Square while driving, you can quickly attack with your car door, as shown:.

This is really useful when you're being flanked by unsuspecting bikers — or you just want to show cyclists who's king the road!

Much like the above car door attack, you can kick any nearby enemies by pushing Square while you're riding a bike, as shown:.

This can help you knock rival motorcylists off their bike, or just give you a good core workout while on the highway.

You can go first-person at any time while you're on-foot and stationary by holding L2 and pressing R3:.

You can move the camera around from this position and press R2 to zoom, but you do need to hold L2 down throughout.

It's also worth noting you can't move while doing this, as there's no traditional first-person mode in the game.

This can be useful for reading signs and other looking closely at other objects in the game, though.

Every vehicle has a full suite of options you can access by holding Left and using the right analogue stick to navigate up to Vehicle, as shown:.

These options can include everything from winding down your windows to turning on your headlights. Speaking of which, you can also toggle your headlights at any time by pressing Circle:.

And, if you're in a boat, you can use the above vehicle management options to set down an anchor, which will keep it in place while you go diving:.

If you're playing on the PS5, the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers will help you observe the speed limit.

It has been revealed that while you're driving, holding R2 until you feel the first point of resistance. This is the speed limit.

You'll need to have Adaptive Triggers Resistance enabled to feel this, and you can check it's on by pressing Options > Settings > Controller > DualSense Wireless Controller Features:.

You can take two cars when you're with your partner by using the command menu.

Hold Right to bring up the menu and press Cross/X to instruct your partner to drive:.

Then get in another car and hold Right again then press Square to follow you:.

You'll notice that your partner will drive right behind you, which can be useful if you need to setup getaway cars during robberies:.

Did you know about any or all of these secret controls in GTA 6? You can find even more tips and tricks through the link, as well as tons of collectible and mission walkthroughs in our GTA 6 guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

Sources indicate that the BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

It has been revealed that kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

Industry observers note that kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the firm contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

It has been revealed that cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has managed to get its claws into just about everyone. Honestly, I can't go anywhere without hearing something from the soundtrack or someone talking about how much fun it is to joyride around Leonida. And now it's even infested the sports I watch.

To keep non-Formula One fans up to speed, it was the Las Vegas Grand Prix over the weekend, one of the newer circuits on the calendar. Third place went to Oscar Piastri. In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race.

"I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he says in a stream (via IGN), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around.".

Verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't.".

GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing the game, the only difference being that instead of subsequently competing in an F1 race and winning it, I spend the next day of work acting like a zombie—a poorly functioning one at that. I suppose people are just built differently, or at least that's what I'll tell myself while I'm on my third cup of coffee in three hours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it might be hard to believe now, but Bethesda wasn't everyone's top choice for bringing back the Fallout series. In fact, when it came to Fallout 3, Obsidian was the studio many fans wanted to see tackle the wasteland, emboldening the team behind The Elder Scrolls to get things right for the sci-fi RPG.

Industry observers note that bruce Nesmith, a long-time developer at Bethesda who worked on Skyrim and the Fallout games (including as a quest designer on Fallout 3), explained the atmosphere back in the mid-to-late 2000s to The Examined Game. "There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout license to do Fallout 3," he remembers.

According to recent reports, "There were a lot of people who were Obsidian fans who were like, 'Bethesda's going to screw it up, they're just going to make it [Oblivion], we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout, these guys should never have had it,'" he notes. "There was a strong vocal community that just hated that we were going to make that game.".

It has been revealed that if you can cast your mind back to the era, Obsidian would've seemed like a more appealing choice. Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords in 2004 proved the team's ability to handle sprawling science-fiction, and Bethesda's push into open-world design didn't quite blend with the nuance of the early Fallout releases.

But Todd Howard and his crew weren't about to let the doubters win. If anything, they became more dedicated to making Fallout 3. "We had to prove them wrong," Nesmith notes. "And fortunately, we did. And Fallout 3 was embraced, even by a lot of our skeptics.".

He mentions there was a portion of the fanbase who maintain that Fallout 2 was the franchise highlight, and will forever remain so. "But we tried our best to just not engage. You're not going to win that argument, you're not going to persuade hearts and minds," he adds. "All you can do is make the best game you can make and let that be your statement.".

And Fallout 3 is quite the statement. Obsidian did give us Fallout: Upcoming Vegas in 2010, and then we got Fallout 4 from Bethesda in 2015. When will we see Fallout 5? That's anyone's guess, but Obsidian is apparently working on another game set in the wasteland for the time-being.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.

Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.

Xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly. Just a few months ago, I bought Subnautica 2 to play with a friend through the Xbox PC app. I could've opted for Steam, but I wanted to work towards those Xbox cheevos (when they eventually arrive). For a couple of weeks, I'd hop on the PC and dive into alien waters with my mate.

Recent findings suggest that one day, I fancied playing on the big screen in my living room, so I installed Subnautica 2 on my Xbox Series X, booted it up and was prompted to buy a Game Pass subscription just to play the same save file I'd been enjoying for weeks through the Xbox PC app. Like I mentioned, a bit silly.

Time went on, and I'd more or less let this go from my head until I read a report from Windows Central a couple days ago, claiming that Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix next-gen console could have prepares to kill paywalls for paid multiplayer.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer.".

According to Jez Corden, the original strategy for Xbox Helix was to create a console-PC hybrid with access to Steam, potentially spelling the end of Xbox's staple multiplayer charges. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. If you can play your Xbox games across both console and PC, whether through disc-to-digital or Xbox Play Anywhere, it seems like pointless friction to lock multiplayer behind a paywall depending on which device you're playing on.

In a recent development, back in 2021, changes to Xbox's paid multiplayer requirements allowed players without an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to access multiplayer free-to-play titles such as Fortnite, Call of Duty: Warzone and Apex Legends. And today, Xbox Live Gold isn't even a thing, as it's been absorbed into Xbox Game Pass.

So, even if Xbox Helix's original vision has changed somewhat from what Corden initially reported, it's still not out of the question to suggest that paid multiplayer could eventually become redundant.

As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

Industry observers note that you'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and new buttons let you promptly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," stated Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive.".

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free upgrade and will be available on all platforms.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio noted it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Enhancement. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash.

There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above shows a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch.

If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town. You can also get a winched truck around the back of Yasmani's vape shop in Little Cuba—the fence who gives you the ATM tip offs.

Industry observers note that you'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them.

For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't revealed a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming states is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially announced.

If Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

According to recent reports, complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an update introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and latest skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a new high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

Did anyone really think The Witcher 4 was going to be a PS5 exclusive?

For those who missed it, CDPR confirmed yesterday that it has signed a marketing deal with Sony on its upcoming RPG.

While the details are light, it’s expected this will take the same shape as PlayStation’s arrangement with GTA 6, where the title’s promoted “like” an exclusive – even though it’s technically not.

But it seems there was some confusion online about the nature of Sony’s deal, which CEO Michal Nowakowski has now clarified on social media.

Sources indicate that “We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform.”.

It’s as expected really, but Nowakowski still faced follow-up questions about whether Ciri’s story may launch first on PS5, before other platforms.

“All the platforms release at the same time: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. No one gets left behind.”.

Of course, this is all entirely as expected – the original comments mentioned a marketing deal only, and I don’t think Sony could afford to keep a game as major as The Witcher 4 off other platforms, to be brutally honest.

It does hopefully mean the game will be optimised for the PS5, though, taking advantage of unique features like the DualSense et al.

I’m sure we’ll learn a lot more about how Sony and CDPR are collaborating once we get closer to the game’s release.

According to recent reports, prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a latest version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

According to recent reports, originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

"This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent company Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

Over the last few days, I've been running into various bits of discussion on social media about how GTA 6 is crashing or even "frying" some people's consoles, and for the most part it's been talked about in regards to the PS5 version.

This particular clip has been getting a ton of attention this week (profanity warning):.

The Verge editor Tom Warren ended up picking up on this, suggesting that "GTA 6 is really stress testing the GPUs inside consoles", and then pointing out that the Xbox Support Reddit community highlights complications on Xbox as well.

And after visiting it, yeah... there's no doubt it's got multiple reports from people who claim GTA 6 has been responsible for either crashing their console or putting stress on the GPU and causing the visuals to stop functioning properly.

Here are just a few examples of people confirming their issues:.

Now, as scary as this might seem, it's worth keeping in mind that you're unlikely to run into any major issues. The majority of GTA 6 players are enjoying the game just fine on their Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S and PS5 consoles right now, and I'm willing to bet most people haven't had a single crash whatsoever.

It also should be noted that Rockstar aimed to reduce crashes in their latest revision for GTA 6 this week.

In a recent development, at the same time, it's also impossible to say how widespread the problem is, but most people speculate that it's limited to anywhere between 0.1% and 5% of Xbox players at most. GTA 6 is an incredibly demanding game without a doubt, and it might unfortunately be exposing some weaknesses in certain consoles for whatever reason.

Industry observers note that that's why we're only saying "a small number of" consoles in the headline here, because we don't want you to get scared off from playing GTA 6 over the next few weeks and months. Just keep in mind that it's a good idea to ensure your console isn't too clogged up with dust every now and again, and hopefully you'll never run into complications like this.

Sources indicate that we know that Pokémon Winds and Waves will launch on Switch 2 at some point in 2027, but that's it. The Pokémon Company is still keeping quiet about the upcoming Gen 10 entry, but an revealed gap in the long-running anime has some people already narrowing the release window.

Earlier today, it was declared that the Pokémon anime would be taking a whopping nine-month gap between the finale of 'Winter Voyage' in December and a newly introduced series starring Liko and Roy, which kicks off in October 2027.

Serebii's Joe Merrick was quick to point out that the anime typically doesn't take breaks like this — usually airing an episode a week, bar some minor gaps. Given that fresh series of the show typically launch alongside their mainline game, does this mean that there has been a scheduling change at The Pokémon Company, with Winds and Waves being pushed back until later in the year?

According to recent reports, it certainly seems like a delay behind closed doors is possible — it is strange that TPC would schedule a gap this massive in the anime run intentionally. If the upcoming series is set to tie in with Gen 10, then that would put Winds and Waves launching sometime around October 2027.

Hell, any extra time that TPC can be developing the next mainline title gets a major thumbs up from us.

Of course, it could also just be a wild intended pause in the anime, which had no sway on the game at all. TPC always eyes up the big pre-holiday November window for its mainline releases, so who's to say Gen 10 would ever have been any different?

Or things could be really off the wall, and this scheduled anime series is actually nothing to do with Winds and Waves, which TPC could go crazy and release any other time in the year instead!

In short, we're still waiting on something concrete from The Pokémon Tech giant before we know the next release date for sure. But if this anime start date is anything to go by, we imagine we'll be seeing Gen 10 in the same November window that we're used to.

When do you think we'll see Pokémon Winds and Waves launch on Switch 2? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The lack of an official GTA 6 launch on PC hasn't stopped fans from attempting to tackle one themselves, with many projects allegedly making quick progress toward a working version of Rockstar's behemoth – and, now, multiplayer, too.

Sources indicate that in case you're out of the loop, this is all being tracked on PortWatch – a platform dedicated to updating folks with progress on every unofficial PC port at the moment in development. As of now, the website claims we're 91.3% of the way to seeing one fully come to fruition… but that's not the most eye-catching news on there. Late last night, PortWatch reported that "GTA 6 multiplayer is running on PC." Yes, multiplayer.

"TeK's group has players, cars and proximity voice chat working at a stable 25 to 30 fps, on a private fork of CGBJ's build," their revision reads. "PortWatch has verified the video is real." For reference, "TeK's group" is one of the teams heading the (again, unofficial) race to get GTA 6 on PC. Apparently, their take on multiplayer features "player characters and vehicles together in the world, with proximity voice chat, so you hear the players near you." It is "private," of course, but still – this is sort of mind-boggling, as PortWatch notes. "Until now, every build we track has been single-player: getting GTA 6's story to run on PC at all has taken everyone's effort. Multiplayer means separate copies of the game agreeing on where every player and car is, and no build on our board had shown that before." Especially seeing as there's been no word from Rockstar on GTA 6 Online.

Industry observers note that all of this started with notorious GTA 6 leaker "Cyberleek," who uploaded an executable file for the Xbox build of the game they previously dropped online. That's when groups like TeK picked it up and began working toward a PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6. It's not the only feat fans have taken upon themselves, either. As per VideoCardz, we've seemingly got mods popping up now, too – a possibility that previously felt uncertain thanks to Rockstar's anti-cheat software.

Recent findings suggest that in other words, there's a lot going on right now – but, yet another disclaimer, none of it's official… and it's likely that Rockstar will eventually crack down when things start going live and public (should they do so). Here's hoping we get an actual PC launch someday, though.

💡 Key Takeaways
