  • It has been revealed that it was looking like there really wouldn't be any way out of the danger Irwin (Miles Teller), his brother Gary (Adam Driver) and his family were in.
  • It has been revealed that after seeing his brother one last time at Scott's birthday party, Gary lies and states he's leaving the country, assuring Irwin things are going to be ok and gifting him his car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To say that Paper Tiger had me stressed would be an understatement. James Gray's crime drama, which just arrived on the 2026 movie schedule, had me on the edge of my seat throughout, and then reeling from those final scenes. I want to get into what happened at the end of the movie, and what the writer/director told us about it. I can't do that without 🛑 MAJOR spoilers from the Adam Driver movie - if you haven't seen Paper Tiger and have somehow wandered into this article, now's your chance to leave! Be sure to catch it in theaters or wait until it's available on streaming.

It has been revealed that it was looking like there really wouldn't be any way out of the danger Irwin (Miles Teller), his brother Gary (Adam Driver) and his family were in. Gary, as it turned out, wasn't the kind of cop who would cross major ethical lines by working with the Russian mob - at least not for any kind of job that isn't above board. When money wasn't going to be enough to satisfy Simeon Bogoyavich (Victor Ptak), and Gary wasn't willing to work with him, the only way to make things right was for Gary to accept the terms of Simeon's deal: his life in exchange for his brother's (and his family's) safety. That was Simeon's price, and Gary agreed to pay it.

It has been revealed that after seeing his brother one last time at Scott's birthday party, Gary lies and states he's leaving the country, assuring Irwin things are going to be ok and gifting him his car. We see him get emotional when he's by himself in his rental car, which I interpret as him accepting his fate, as terrible as it is.

Recent findings suggest that later, he drives toward the airport and waits until he sees the Russian guys tailing him. He mutters something about wanting to take them out with him, and then pulls off to the side of the road, where he hides in a nearby field. The guys creep around among the stalks and Gary shoots a couple of them, the gunshot sounds muffled by the planes overhead. He's inevitably shot by one of them and dies.

At Irwin's house, his wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) has snuck off to have surgery on her brain tumor. She's last seen blowing a kiss to her husband and kids, who are still asleep. Later that morning, Scott is helping Ben study, and Irwin listens to a message about job opportunities now that his and his brother's consulting business is registered. The tone is uplifting in the Pearl house, despite what we know. Does this mean that everything is going to be ok, and the Russian mob boss will keep his end of the deal now that Gary is dead?

As writer/director James Gray told us, he has hope that things will be ok for the family.

Industry observers note that I think they're going to be all right. Somehow I have hope. You get he gets a message that this the better business or the business bureau or whatever it is, is going to has all this great jobs lined up for him and his children are studying for school very dutifully.

In the final scene within the Pearl house, they don't yet know about Hester's situation, though it seems unlikely that she'll keep that a secret for long. This family may be out of the woods with this Russian mob situation, but that doesn't mean everything will be perfect in the coming weeks and months. As Gray put it:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I mean, he's got something terrible coming with his wife that he doesn't know about, right? But that's life. You know, bad things and good things happen in equal measure. We almost have to kind of accept that that's what our fates are as human beings. But I think he'll be all right.

The more I think about Paper Tiger's ending, the more this makes sense to me and adds to my overall satisfaction to this suspenseful and emotional film. Hester's tumor is nobody's doing, just the tragic nature of life, unfair though it may be. So much of what transpired in the film had to do with choices and actions, but in the case of Hester, it's just the cards she was dealt, and she and her family will have to face that.

Industry observers note that I did personally feel a note of hope in that final scene. Because Irwin and his sons weren't aware of what happened to Gary, or what was going in with Hester, they were just going about their morning routines. It felt like we were seeing a glimpse of what everyday life would look like for these three Pearl men, and it was simple and safe. It's the calm before another storm, but there's a note of optimism that they'll get through it and have each other for support.

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player states they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 mentioned they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

Industry observers note that "Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found.".

According to recent reports, in a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety says that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and notes Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt.

Crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

Stealing the Pegassi Infernus in GTA 6 can be quite tricky, considering it's being held in the police department lockup, the building to the west of the police station in southwest Crosstown.

You can access the building via a yellow window cleaning elevator on the southern side of the building. But this won't appear until Randy texts and gives you the Infernus's location. If you go here before, your options for entering are far more limited and risky, so it's worth waiting. To get to the car:.

Now you just need to drive down a few levels to exit via the police station parking lot—which I'd recommend—or keep going all the way down to exit at the bottom of the car park. Remember, you need to drive fast to stop the tracker going off, and if you hear it beeping, you should speed up to prevent it pinging the cops.

It has been revealed that if you do bash around the car a bit, you can get it repaired at a gas station on the way. Bring it back in pristine condition and you'll net 15k for the trouble.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As with nearly every offer in Sony's digital store, there are literally thousands of PS5 and PS4 games going cheap.
  • We've put together a (relatively) shorter list of some of the games we'd highly recommend while they're on offer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The PS Store's Black Friday sale is on now, running until 30th November, 2026.

As with nearly every offer in Sony's digital store, there are literally thousands of PS5 and PS4 games going cheap. Obviously, nobody has the time to scroll through all those deals, which is where this guide hopefully comes in handy.

We've put together a (relatively) shorter list of some of the games we'd highly recommend while they're on offer.

Everything listed here comes with at least a 7/10 score from Push Square, and every game is at its lowest price point, with some setting fresh lows in this sale.

Discounted prices are shown in bold, and games at a fresh lowest-ever price are bold and underlined.

If you need to top up your PSN wallet, we've got you covered:.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Let's have a look at some of the best games in the Black Friday sale.

The best James Bond game in a very long time, 007 First Light revives the character in brilliant style. Telling the origin story of the would-be spy, the game is a combination of sandbox-like, open-ended missions and linear set pieces and narrative moments, resulting in a highly appealing blockbuster. It tells a decent story, establishes fantastic new takes on well-known characters, and sets a solid foundation with great espionage and action gameplay.

1000xRESIST is all in on story, and this laser focus allows it to tell one of the most captivating and intriguing experiences you can have in video games. This sci-fi adventure sees an alien disease almost wipe out humanity, but one person is immune, and they rebuild society underground by cloning her. Combining visual novel elements with exploration, it's not the most challenging game to play, but its narrative more than makes it worthwhile.

It has been revealed that if you're looking for a chilled out puzzle game to wind down with, A Monster's Expedition comes highly recommended. It's one of those puzzlers with a seemingly straightforward set of mechanics, but it uses them in increasingly smart ways to really test your brainpower. Set across hundreds of tiny islands you need to navigate by pushing logs into the water, its forgiving nature and gentle presentation make it a lovely game to get lost in.

In a recent development, A whimsical, miniature open world awaits in A Short Hike. From a top-down perspective, you explore an island with lots of interesting places to visit and adorable characters, each of whom has a task for you. This laid back experience is a true joy as you gain new abilities, collect things, and discover new areas.

Recent findings suggest that absolum is both a brilliantly crafted beat-'em-up and a devilishly addictive roguelike. Although the overall experience does feel slightly short-lived, you'll seriously struggle to tear yourself away from the game's striking fantasy world — especially when all of its systems start to click.

ARC Raiders is a phenomenal showcase of what immersive multiplayer can be. Every run is different, and your squad will come out with stories to tell each time. It can be tougher on those planning to play solo, and the extraction loop won't be for everyone. But as far as extraction shooters go, this is one of the most accessible, and it respects your time, giving you a fun experience from your first match. We can easily say that ARC Raiders is one of the best multiplayer games this generation.

According to recent reports, arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is a delightfully inventive puzzle game that weaves in a neat narrative to pull you through. Playing as a character that literally moves the world around her as she goes, this is effectively a series of slide puzzles set within a fleshed out world full of whimsical character. Always building on its core idea in imaginative ways, this is brilliant fun from start to finish.

Building upon the great foundations laid in Astro's Playroom, Astro Bot is the full-blown 3D platformer the little robot deserves. It's an explosion of creativity and fun; there is something latest to discover in practically every level, and all of it is purpose built to put a smile on your face. Not only is it bursting with imagination, it's also executed brilliantly. The controls are spot on, every new mechanic and power-up is fun to use, and it's all presented with incredibly sharp visuals and flawless performance. The icing on the cake is its celebration of PlayStation's past 30 years, with delightful nods to hundreds of classics. We can't recommend this highly enough.

It has been revealed that while many of the included games may border on unplayable from a modern perspective, the painstaking attention to detail in Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is extremely easy to appreciate. The museum-like carousel of content, from interviews through to original artwork, is presented so handsomely that you can’t not get swept up in Atari’s dramatic story. And the fact that there over 100 of the manufacturer’s most famous titles, emulated excellently with their original instruction manuals available to pore over, adds playable context to a lot of the content. This is just an impressive overall experience that will appeal to those who lived through the rise (and fall) of Atari, as well as younger players eager to learn a little more about one of the industry’s true pioneers.

In a recent development, avowed is arguably Obsidian's strongest modern release, and it's not for the reasons that you may think. While the game's writing and storytelling often lack bite and excitement, its gameplay saves the day with a cracking combat system, meaningful player choice, and the enjoyable exploration of some truly stunning locales.

Recent findings suggest that ball X Pit is a dangerously addictive roguelite that combines the speedy runs and rapid leveling up of Vampire Survivors with the ball-bouncing action of Breakout. It's one of those concepts that'll make you question why a game like it hasn't been done before, because it works brilliantly. Every element of the game feeds into something else, and the result is this incredibly compelling game that has a surprising amount to see and do.

It has been revealed that battle Chef Brigade Deluxe is the definitive version of this unusual but great culinary adventure. Set in a world where chefs go head-to-head in a prestigious cooking tournament, the game is half action title and half cooking minigames. You'll go out slaying monsters and harvesting ingredients, then brew them up to create delicious dishes to satisfy the judges. It's an odd recipe, but results in a surprisingly tasty dish.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 is a phenomenal multiplayer experience that immerses and impresses with its chaotic mix of tight gunplay, best-in-class audio design, and the cinematic flair that made us love the series in the first place. The campaign isn’t anything to write home about, and Portal has yet to fully prove its worth, but they act as additions to what is easily the best Battlefield in over a decade.

Recent findings suggest that A true cult classic, Beyond Good & Evil: 20th Anniversary Edition is a lovely remaster of a PS2 favourite. Playing as freedom fighter Jade, this unique sci-fi adventure has you exploring a weird and wonderful world through the lens of her camera. The remaster brings the visuals up to date and throws in some quality-of-life improvements, but the main reason to play this is for the great story and characters, which remain fresh and charming to this day.

Industry observers note that broken Sword: Shadow of the Templars is a sacred text in the history of point-and-click adventure games, and newly introduced remaster Reforged is the best version of the game that's ever been released. Quality-of-life improvements mean players who just want to enjoy the story without too much lateral thinking can do so, while veterans of the genre or returning fans can play the game in its original form, goats and all. Paris in the fall has never been more beautiful.

Industry observers note that there have been climbing games before, but Cairn is a really unique example. To scale the huge Mount Kami, you need to control Aava's limbs individually, looking out for the best holds as you inch upward. On top of the challenging, physics-based mountaineering, you also need to keep on top of her health and hunger, but these survival aspects never feel too overbearing. It's a nicely balanced game with climbing that feels tangible and realistically tough.

Industry observers note that half interactive story, half cube-based puzzler, Catherine: Full Body is the expanded remaster of Atlus' brilliantly weird take on love. You play as Vincent, a 32-year-old bachelor who can't quite decide if he wants to commit to his long-term girlfriend. His potential infidelity gives way to suspiciously vivid nightmares where he's forced to scramble up towers made of blocks, lest he wake up dead. It's as mental as it sounds, but the tactile puzzles are addictive, and the storytelling is gripping at its best.

From the makers of TowerFall Ascension, Celeste is a pure platformer that provides a stern challenge. Using a straightforward set of moves, it does a lot with very little, but it's not just gameplay where it impresses. Madeline's climb up Celeste Mountain is both literal and metaphorical as she struggles to overcome her inner demons. Wonderfully pairing a touching story with rock solid platforming, this is one indie adventure that'll stay with you.

Sources indicate that creaks is one of PS4's very best puzzle games. Its commitment to continually evolving its mechanics makes for a phenomenal puzzling experience packed full of surprises and elating moments. With a stunning art style to boot as well as a narrative which reveals itself in all the right ways, Creaks offers an unforgettable ride that can be considered truly special.

Some say there are too many Metroidvania games for this world, yet when one as good as Crypt Custodian comes along, it serves as a reminder of exactly why so many developers chase that addictive fusion of explorative action. With shades of Death's Door and Tunic, brotherly duo Kyle and Eric Thompson have made an approachable yet exceedingly enjoyable adventure full of combat, platforming, puzzles, and charm.

Masterful in its storytelling, characters, and visuals, Kojima Productions went bigger and better with a sequel that comfortably dwarfs what the Japanese team achieved in its first delivery experience. Main character Sam is once again tasked with reconnecting a land mass to the chiral network, but this time his deliveries are further and expanded to encompass proper combat scenarios. Death Stranding 2 is a cinematic achievement on all fronts that will remain one of the crown jewels of the PS5 library forever.

In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.

It has been revealed that referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects". As of writing, the legitimacy of the executable doesn't appear to have been independently verified, meaning it could still just turn out to be a pile of malware or something similarly dodgy. Industry observers note that cyberleek have been bigging up the idea that these files they've been releasing could result in GTA 6 running on PC sharpish, via a modified version cobbled together with generative AI. That might happen, but I'm seriously skeptical that if it were to, it wouldn't just be dodgy jankware than runs like piss, rather than anything that'd compare remotely well to an official PC port.

Thus far, it appears a group of would-be recompilers going by Project Leonida may have got the game to start booting on PC, but they since look to have disappeared and scrubbed their established online presence.

All of this again raises the question of whether the threat of any sort of bodged PC recreation coming out of this alleged executable release may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between this month's console release and its eventual Windows release, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year.

Recent findings suggest that returning to Cyberleek's latest statement, the leaker or leakers have also taken the opportunity to insist that their attempts to pump up a crypto coin as part of the leaking is just for practical reasons rather than grifty ones, honest. "Every donation is a vote for more of this," they wrote. "Where the votes go, [Cyberleek] follows. Crypto here is just a tool - there is no other way to move funds without names.".

Rockstar called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking". Along with parent company Take-Two, they began a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August, but that doesn't seem to to have deterred Cyberleek, if indeed the people leaking under the name are still the same ones as in the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing new data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella said on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active customers] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

GTA 6 debuted on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

In a recent development, eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Piracy has been the scourge of the anime and manga industries for decades. Now, the Japanese government is clamping down on those sailing into illegal seas on the internet with "AI agents.".

As per Yomiuri (H/T Automaton Media) Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs has trialled the AI detection system over the past year on both Twitter and across the wider internet.

In recent years, it has been confirmed that piracy to anime, manga and games in Japan costs the industries north of $35 billion dollars, a figure almost equivalent to what they bring in revenue each year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 hasn't even been out for a week yet, and someone has already done the math on how many buildings in the whole of Leonida you can actually walk into. For those of you who are curious: it's 1,563 buildings.

That is frankly ridiculous. I don't think I've ever been inside 1,563 different buildings in my entire life, although I am a creature of habit, so that could explain things. The player who shared these stats, Aileos, does note that there are 5,588 buildings in total, so the enterable buildings only account for a fraction of that, just over 25%.

According to recent reports, there are some who will look at this with a glass-half-empty perspective, and I get it. This world is so cool, it's easy to want more of it, but as another player points out, "This would've sent us into psychosis a few years back". Sometimes it's better to focus on what we have rather than what we don't have. After all, how many buildings will you realistically enter in your GTA 6 playthrough? Probably not 1,563.

We've spent the past week here in the PC Gamer Slack channel marvelling at just how many random encounters you can stumble across in GTA 6. Some of us have found sentient NPCs. One of us was actually recognised by a convenience store clerk who then asked to get robbed, and I think we've all seen videos of the furry rescue mission.

It has been revealed that but just because this world already has loads of awesome activities, it doesn't mean we aren't hoping for more. A massive casino and go-kart track have been spotted by players, both of which have huge "Coming Soon" signs draped outside of them.

These buildings could be lying in wait for GTA 6 Online, or they could be added to singleplayer sometime in the future. Regardless, those are two more buildings that will potentially welcome players soon.

Following the full game list for Awesome Games Done Quick being released a little while ago, GDQ have now published the full schedule for the event running for a week from January 3rd through January 10th in Atlanta (and streamed on Twitch, of course). Included amongst the latest games this year are 2026 releases like Queen's Domain, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Ocarina of Time remake, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which all make a lot of sense as games practically made for speedrunning. Belmont's Curse, specifically, is set to be the event's final bonus game, only to be played if donation incentives are met (which I'm sure they will be, it's a Castlevania game at GDQ).

Industry observers note that but then, there's also Substantial Walk, which I'm fascinated by the prospect of trying to speedrun as a group. It's listed as a '12 player showcase', which I can only imagine denotes it as more of a fun experiment to put on a show, rather than a world-record aiming speedrun. The chaos of twelve people trying to work together in Big Walk live on the GDQ stage is a spectacle that has my interest, either way. Also making the cut is train-flipping stunt game Denshattack!, which I simply have to mention got a resounding "✨🚂DENSHATTACK MENTIONED🚂✨" from James in the RPS chat this morning. I can't help but share his excitement, in fairness, since Denshattack! is just that cool.

According to recent reports, as for some of the more out-there picks, which I say entirely positively, there's a run of not the DmC reboot, but specifically its bonus Vergil DLC, which is the first time I've heard that mentioned in years. Metroid Prime Origins, a fangame that 'demakes' the famously first-person Metroid Prime into a 2D sidescroller more akin to Zero Mission, is also on the cards; lovely to think there'll be a latest speedrun for a new Metroid game just a month before Ravenous comes out. And finally, on a personal note because of my own biases, I'm deeply interested to see the Any% run of Yakuza 5 play out; that game is infamous for its ridiculous scope and length, so watching a runner try to get it down to only its most essential parts should be a treat. The schedule estimates around 2 hours for the run, to which I can only say good luck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True was filmed at Disney World and mostly at night. Yes, this new Hallmark movie was filmed at Disney World and at night. So, while the experience was magical, the cast and crew of this project on the 2026 Christmas movie schedule kind of had to turn into vampires to survive. With that in mind, I had to ask the movie’s star, Lacey Chabert, and her colleagues what exactly it was like to film in the most magical place on Earth during the hours of the day when most people are fast asleep.

While working in the parks after hours must have been an exciting prospect for the cast of Holiday Ever After, in practice it took a bit to get used to it. They were working through the night instead of the day, and according to Philip actor Travis Van Winkle, it took a second to adjust to that:.

It has been revealed that it takes a second for your whole body to adjust to that, but once you do, you become a vampire. And it's kind of nice being awake at four in the morning, and you're just wide awake, and you know, excited to film a scene. And then to watch the sunrise every morning at Disney World when no one's in the park. I mean, it was very surreal that happened every night, every morning.

Sam actor Bryce Durfee and producer David Wulf also brought up how they kind of felt like vampires making this movie. Durfee specifically noted that staying awake sometimes was legitimately hard, and that is what led to this back-and-forth:.

Executive producer Jennifer Aspen made it very clear that what these actors pulled off with these night shoots was “pretty exceptional.” That’s because, not only were they working on vampire hours, they also had to make sure everything got done before the sun came up and the crowds came in.

To that point, Wulf said that behind the scenes they were “communicating with every element of the parks” to make sure they got the most “amazing moment for Hallmark” without “interfering with the guest experience.” Meanwhile, while they were capturing all of that, the cast also got to experience the magic of Disney World.

Industry observers note that thankfully, the cast aren’t really vampires, and they could see the sunrise each morning on set (which, again, was Disney World). Lacey Chabert, who plays Lindsey in the movie, told me that was her favorite part of these night shoots too. After saying the parks were “magical” during that time, she also stated:.

According to recent reports, my favorite moment was when we would finish our night shoot, then we would shoot some daytime things early in the morning, seeing the park open. The music starts. They make an announcement. Rope drop happens. People run in, and it's just this infectious excitement and joy. And I hope that all of that comes through the movie. I know that it does.

The Mean Girls actress also explained that those magical feelings were there as they were getting ready for their night shoots, too. That’s because, as they were getting ready, the parks were preparing to close, and Magic Kingdom’s fireworks would be happening:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, yeah, and our base camp was in the parking lot of Magic Kingdom, and usually our call time was about 9 o'clock, so we could watch the fireworks from the makeup trailer. I mean, once in a lifetime.

Actors get to have surreal filming experiences all the time. However, getting ready while the fireworks go off is seriously iconic.

Taegen Burns (she plays Kiera) also used the word “magical” to describe this whole experience too. She explained that despite the “wonky hours,” getting to be in the parks without other people was “incredible.”.

In a recent development, so, now that I’ve quoted so many positive adjectives the cast used, it’s clear that feeling like vampires while filming this entry on the 2026 TV schedule didn’t bother them much. And if it did, the magical nature of being at Disney World made up for it.

Now, to see what they made during the wee hours of the night in the most magical place on earth, you can catch Holiday Every After on the Hallmark Channel on Saturday, November 28 at 8 p.m. ET, and you can stream it the next day on Hallmark+ or with a Hulu or Disney+ subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicalis has removed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest patch, prompting a wave of negative reviews on Steam.

According to recent reports, the music in question was tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6, which rolled out on the same day (19th November). A day later, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted that the run's music was "100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof)", pointing to tracks that reference the AI music tool Suno in their metadata.

"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one Steam review reads (thanks, IGN).

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds [for] refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," said another.

Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

Responding to the criticism, Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen mentioned he "woke up to a shit show".

It has been revealed that "Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he wrote on X/Twitter, before inviting players to report concerns and bugs to the email address shared in one of Nicalis' tweets, which confirmed it had "pushed a new build with critical fixes", including the "removal of generated music files". The patch is live on PC, and Nicalis says it has been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony.

Nicalis has yet to explain how the music ended up in the game.

Hi All!Repentance+ Revision:The team has pushed a new build with critical fixes.• Removal of generated music files• Larynx + Car Battery Bug Fix• PC patch—should be live already• Submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo and Sony ASAPAdditional: • Continuing work on netcode… pic.twitter.com/d1gyLUlBK8.

Industry observers note that following the gigantic Afterbirth and Afterbirth+ expansions, released in 2015 and 2017 respectively, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth grew again with 2021's community-inspired, sequel-sized Repentance DLC. That was meant to be the last content drop for real, yet 2024 gave us the free Repentance+ DLC, which finally added online co-op to the disturbingly charming roguelike. The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth has since hit a latest concurrent player record on Steam 12 years after it was released.

McMillen's most recent game, Mewgenics, also made quite a splash earlier this year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Atari Homebrew Awards, an annual celebration of upcoming games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.

Industry observers note that "As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums.

According to recent reports, "Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of newly introduced AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.

"The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the new fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I rapidly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought.".

James noted he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code.".

That left two options: Disallow any and all AI usage in the Atari Homebrew Awards competition, which James mentioned would disqualify a large number of "extremely talented coders" who used AI in some very minor way, or let it slide and either choose an arbitrary dividing line between what is and isn't allowed or allow everything, including fully vibe-coded games.

James remarked he wasn't interested in that, which meant he needed to settle on how much AI usage would be allowable—and also how to determine if AI was used at all, since some developers are better at disclosure than others. That, naturally, led to the worry that developers could be subject to "false positives and possible witch hunts," something that's already a problem in mainstream game development.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year.

Ultimately, James decided there was no practical way forward, although he did leave open the possibility of a return someday. "This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year," he wrote. "I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a upcoming normal.".

As we noted in July, debates over "acceptable" levels of AI use are cropping up all over the open source development scene: Some are drawing hard lines against it for principled and/or practical reasons, yet its popularity is growing explosively because, frankly, you don't need to know what you're doing in order to do it—as long as you're not too concerned with doing it well.

In a recent development, the Atari Homebrew Awards isn't the first such event to fall victim to the AI flood. Earlier in November, the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a "free national videogame development competition for students," announced that the 2026 event will be its last because "the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development [made] it harder to judge what students made themselves," and thus undercut the whole purpose of the program: Encouraging kids to learn how to code.

It has been revealed that despite being announced back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now. That seems to have changed, however, as the release date on its Steam page has slipped to 2027 without any sort of announcement as to why.

In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.

Industry observers note that based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice. When I played a demo at Gamescom 2026, I was a little stunned by how awful it felt to play. The protagonist was a blank slate designed to be pretty and nothing more, and the combat was mind-numbingly oversimplified, its challenge mainly derived from the need to wrestle with its janky controls and the noticeable delay between button presses and attacks. In that same interview, Luo notes an awareness of the game being compared to the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series in being a 'wacky' open-world action RPG, saying that he's "happy that players are making that association", as "it means they've recognised Showa American Story as a rich RPG with plenty of content to sink their teeth into." I can respect him taking the comparison in stride, but what I played seemed like a pale imitation of LAD that missed what makes that series more than it seems on the surface.

I can hope that this delay can result in improvements to the critiques the game has faced — Luo did mention that "we've heard many valuable comments regarding the feel of the controls and how the action is presented" — and that Showa American Story releases in a good state sometime in 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

It has been revealed that "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries noted. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves.".

Game writer Michael Wiafe mentioned Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe mentioned. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them.".

Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it.".

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Recent findings suggest that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have announced Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.

Symphony of War II: Dominion Announcement Trailer | Strategy RPG Watch on YouTube.

According to recent reports, dominion's premise mirrors its predecessor in setting a band of heroes from a wide variety of classes, with units ranging from heavy knights and light archers to cannon-lighting artillery and even dragons the size of large dogs; I do have to wonder if an actual hooded horse is one of the units. Over 100 different classes are available, with the core of the game being swapping out these units to create the most effective squads of units for each turn-based battle. As before, it's not just a matter of recruiting soldiers and never thinking about them again until their turn arrives; a cared for army is a strong army (Sun Tzu noted that, probably), and nurturing your army with new gear, individual perks and specialisation to make the squad work not only on their own, but as a collective.

In a recent development, phil Hamilton, founder of Dancing Dragon Games, elaborated that "With Symphony of War: Dominion, we’re building on what players loved about the first game while taking the series in a direction we’ve wanted to explore for years. We’re delivering a deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG without sacrificing the feel and flow that made the original special." Symphony of War II: Dominion releases sometime next year, so for now, get thinking about how you'll best take care of your squads. To paraphrase Sun Tzu again, keeping them fed is always a good start.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (418 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a new patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat.
  • Sources indicate that the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November.
  • Sources indicate that the system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a new patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat. The patent describes an AI-driven system that listens in on player voice chat following key gameplay moments and later recreates it using in-game characters.

Sources indicate that the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November. According to the filing and its diagrams, the system is a self-learning neural network that recognises major gameplay moments - such as kills, longshots, deaths and so on - and records the player's reaction and voice chat from the moment just before and then after they happen. These can be as simple as brief celebratory shouts, groans or yells, or as complex as trash talk.

Sources indicate that the system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions. The AI then teaches itself to rapidly identify those when they occur in-game and replicate them.

It has been revealed that although the replicated voice lines don't directly repeat players' own chat, the system does keep a profile of each player it analyses so it can deliver a response tailored to them, including sticking to the same spoken language, which it uses large language models (LLMs) to help identify. The patent describes a filter of sorts to keep NPCs from learning offensive language such as slurs.

According to the patent, the system's reach extends beyond in-game voice chat to also potentially access voice comms from major apps like Discord.

Activision's goal is to create NPCs that can speak naturally, rather than re-use the same pre-recorded lines. The application seems to be limited to multiplayer games, including those with co-op. Think of the generic voice lines spoken by AI-teammates like "cover me" and so on in a PvE game, or the many other similar ones in battle royale and PvP matches that contain dozens or hundreds of players.

Incidentally, the patent talks of replacing those generic messages with learned ones for players who join a match without a microphone, but players can also seemingly allow their in-game avatars to always use generated voices.

As the game industry continues to grapple with the use of generative-AI in game development, Activision's patent seems to be going directly to source, recreating how those LLMs and AI systems got their knowledge to begin with: from humans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that while the fifth Toy Story gave us more insight into Jessie, it also gave us an insane Buzz Lightyear moment that was "heaven" for Tim Allen. The actor is known for his ad-libbing, both in his stand-up and in his sitcoms. Some of his best bits and impressions have made it on screen, and this goes for the toy-centric franchise as well. So naturally when the actor returned for the fifth movie, he saw an opportunity to improvise, but the Toy Story animators hated to see him coming.

Allen stopped by The Tonight Show to dish on all things Toy Story 5, and even answered Jimmy Fallon’s questions about that Buzz Lightyear army moment. The actor was totally on board with voicing 50 characters, but he admits that his excitement received mixed reactions from the animators:.

According to recent reports, the problem with a comedian is that I’m in there doing bits. I’m talking to a foam ball. ‘Cause there’s no other actors, you know? So I’m doing this whole thing and every time you ad-lib in a Toy Story movie, the people have two reactions: ‘oh, that’s funny,’ and next is, ‘darn it.’ Because they’ve already animated some of it, so if I ad-lib they gotta go back and re-do it. So they don’t really like it, but they do like it.

It has been revealed that the actor has been playing the character since the first Toy Story in 1995, and has given Buzz a specific voice that can be "deceptively hard to capture" for writers. So Allen gives the character a little something extra that has paid off in his favor, especially since we can thank the actor for an iconic moment:.

The one I did that I loved. He said, ‘You are a toy!’ And I shut - I said, ‘You are a sad strange little man and you have my pity.’ And that was an ad-lib. They went, ‘Oh God, that’s good. Oh…’.

It’s hard to imagine Toy Story without that moment. Though I can see how that would be frustrating for the animators. Ironically one wish that Allen had nearly came true. He has admitted that he wanted more Buzz, as he felt the character didn't have much in prior films. Allen has jokingly stated this way people won’t remember “a fabric cowboy.”.

According to recent reports, in fact, the actor almost got his wish as Toy Story 5 nearly didn’t have Woody at all. Though we did get a sweet reunion between the pals that would have been missed. While voicing so many parts at once sounds intimating, that’s not how Allen saw it:.

In a recent development, I was in heaven, because there were 50 of me. So they run out, and then he goes, ‘We gotta go this way. We’re Space Rangers.’ The guy at the front. So I ad-libbed the two in the back. I wanted to go, ‘Why is he the leader? How come I can’t be leader?’ The other one goes, ‘Because he’s a Space Ranger and we’re all Space Rangers.’ And then he went back and forth. ‘I see no sign of intelligent life anywhere.’ ‘I see no…’ And I’m laughing my ass off in the studio. The window people are going, ‘No.’ We didn’t get one ad-lib in that thing.

However, this wasn’t the first time we’ve seen a multi-Lightyear performance. There was a moment in Toy Story 2 with several Space Ranger toys on the shelves in Al’s Toy Barn. Then we spent some time with an alternative Buzz who temporarily took our Buzz’s place. Though we hadn’t seen a multi-toy arc quite to this extent, which was everything Allen wanted it to be and more.

Industry observers note that it’s unknown whether we’ll see another Toy Story, or if Allen (or Hanks) would return for a sixth, but a time existed when the third was going to be the last. As long as the story is there, and a chance to improv multiple Buzz Lightyears, I think the actor can easily be swayed back to the sound booth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New Radical Games has had its unannounced project canceled according to a developer, with the studio speculated to have been working on a The Simpsons: Hit & Run remake.

Earlier this year, Simpsons creator Matt Groening casually dropped the news that something to do with The Simpsons: Hit & Run was happening, saying at a D23 panel that "the original game is coming back in some form." This, mixed with Newly introduced Radical's now-deleted LinkedIn hiring post that mentioned "our stylized game" which would naturally fit with The Simpsons, had folks speculating that the studio – partially comprised of devs from OG Hit & Run studio, Radical Entertainment – might be working on a remake.

However, whatever the studio was working on has now unfortunately been scrapped. Darren Evenson – senior game designer at Upcoming Radical Games – posts on LinkedIn saying the devs' latest project "was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations.".

While The Simpsons link is still unconfirmed, Evenson writes "if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power" which is a reference to Scarface – which Radical also worked on a game for. However, this line was famously parodied in The Simpsons when Homer has his giant pile of sugar in the backyard. I could be reading entirely too much into it, but that could be a hint that this was sadly a Hit & Run remaster that was canned.

Recent findings suggest that needless to say, fans aren't happy. "I'm never going to emotionally recover from this," one states on Twitter in response. "Yeah bro is paraphrasing a quote from Homer it's over boys," speculates another.

In a recent development, there's no wonder the news is having such an impact, even without confirmation that a remake was definitely canceled. Sure, GTA 6 is the highest-rated game of all time and people were waiting 13 years for it to come out, but after 23 years, The Simpsons Hit & Run was the real open-world car-stealing game that everyone was waiting to see get a follow-up.

The iconic licensed title is still one of the most beloved games ever made, and fans have been asking for a sequel for decades, but despite its massive success – and reports emerging that there was a sequel in the works – one never came to fruition. The unrelated The Simpsons Game was the only console game the franchise has had since.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've been a fan of Grand Theft Auto for a while, you might have noticed a strange absence in GTA 6. While the game is packed full of different activities, the recurring pastime of darts is missing, having been present in GTA 5, GTA Online, and GTA 4.

It has been revealed that the reason for the lack of darts in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, according to Rockstar North co-studio lead Rob Nelson, it's a simple case of Rockstar having too little time and resources to make it to a high standard.

Industry observers note that nelson told VGC: "The darts one is a contentious one. Even we... You hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to.".

In a recent development, nelson elaborated that since Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar has taken to expanding what were small mini-games into full-on activities. He pointed to basketball in GTA 6 as an example, which you can play in a way that feels like an extension of gameplay with "fluid" movement. Even if it's a relatively small chunk of the game, a lot of time went into making it feel like "a game in its own right", Nelson said. And the same is true of pool.

Sources indicate that "A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn't get to," Nelson mentioned. The studio "didn't have the resources" to include it in the game and have it up to par. "It's better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough," he said.

Even without darts, there are plenty of side activities in Grand Theft Auto 6 that help expand Vice City. This includes diving and treasure hunting and fishing, both of which you unlock near the start of the game. If you're looking for a guide of all there is to do in the game, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough is a good place to start. We've also got a breakdown of all the GTA 6 cheats if you needed an extra hand getting through the game.

Industry observers note that genAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it.".

Industry observers note that nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being important in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually. And that seems to be changing fundamentally." He adds that maintaining a short gap also helps as, to put it simply, "people have short memories, right?" And, unfortunately, he's right; there are so many games coming out that adding something to your wishlist often feels like resigning it to remembering it exists six months later.

Sources indicate that he recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed. But then, he clarifies that the reason it seemed so easy was a lack of care. "There's a reason that every kind of AI slop game feels the same; it's because when you try to make something from zero, AI will multiply your skills, and zero times a thousand is still zero." The people claiming to 'develop' recomps do not care for making a game that feels right, or even one that works; they care only for the short-lived dopamine of being popular on Twitter for fifteen minutes before another slop copy rears its head (and is inevitably revealed to be jankware). Nichiporchik specifies that "game feel is impossible to copy; as long as you have a great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be okay." 'Game feel' is one of the vaguest terms that exists in this field, but I do feel that it refers to something tangible and immediately noticeable when it's gone.

For example, I've recently been replaying the wonderful Celeste, and the 'game feel' of its wavedashing is core to making the practice of blazing through levels so engaging. The wavedash works the same every time, due to precise programming from Extremely OK Games spending time and effort painstakingly ensuring it did in the interest of consistency and unity in movement mechanics. You can't make good art without caring about the quality, even if there are now faster ways to knock together a 'working' game. To borrow an overused but still salient phrase: AI could never.

The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, says it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure.".

FinCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone.

Sources indicate that corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X. "As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music.".

In a recent development, A DOGE appointee who previously raised cybersecurity concerns at the IRS with an API "hackathon" and sought to cancel engineering efforts intended to modernize its systems, Corcos is hosting his little LLM project on Github. It's called Legatum, and he describes it as "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization.".

It has been revealed that as Corcos writes in its readme, Legatum is "largely" built with the use of AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated. While FinCEN addresses its cybersecurity breach, Corcos and his Claude agents have been steadily pushing updates: At time of writing, the latest commit—added just six minutes ago—tweaked some of its AI art.

Among the other half-dozen or so commits in the last three hours are adjustments to map generation, music updates, and—let's see—attempts at stemming "a wave of political concerns and README vandalism" left by Github customers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

Sources indicate that this is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it shows that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The company’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the new Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

[source famitsu.com, via gematsu.com].

💡 Key Takeaways

While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one.".
  • Of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence. Simultaneously, there's a certain something to The Witcher as a series that they feel is difficult to make tangible, but is something they want to ensure they don't lose sight of.

Weber describes the core of a 'Witcher-like' story to be something that "explores the various facets of human nature — a game for adults", which he clarifies doesn't just mean violence or sex, but "treating the player as a mature adult, asking difficult questions without offering easy answers." While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one.".

Of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri. Blacha explains that "Ciri isn't calm and composed like Geralt, nor does she hide her emotions easily. She is far more hot-headed and tends to be emotional when making decisions." In terms of how this actually affects the narrative itself and the protagonist's place in it, he elaborates that "when playing as Geralt, players acted more like an arbiter judging how to resolve a situation. When playing as Ciri, you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective." It's an interesting notion, to state that the difference in role is that where Geralt was more of a fixer, Ciri actually approaches situations on an interpersonal level. Weber seemingly half-jokes that "we find ourselves in a position very similar to Ciri's. Just as Ciri must succeed Geralt, we must create a game that lives up to The Witcher 3.".

As for how The Witcher 4 will play, moment to moment, Weber explains that some inspiration has been taken from Cyberpunk 2077 in regards to its open, player-led approach to customisation and, as a result, quests. "You could be a netrunner or a cyber ninja air-dashing into a scene with a double jump. We had to account for all those possibilities available to the player," he recalls. While I can't imagine Ciri will be air-dashing around Kovir, this statement does make me wonder how this approach can be applied to a game with such a specific existing protagonist, rather than the blank slate of Cyberpunk 2077's V. Recalling the side content of The Witcher 3 and its acclaim, he believes that people loved them "because we strived to offer something fresh" and "didn't create quests that merely waste the player's time", which is a principle that "remains unchanged today." Later, he condenses his feelings into the mantra that "A great quest can stem from a compelling story, an engaging character, or fantastic gameplay alone, but overall, there must be harmony.".

Towards the end of the interview, Blacha jokes that "One of our greatest achievements is convincing people to finish their workday, buy our game, and then clock into another job as a character inside the game." It's quite a long and engaging read, so if you're invested in The Witcher IV and its narrative development, I do encourage you read the entire thing.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that if you take a look at Metacritics' best games of all time list, you'll see Grand Theft Auto 6 sitting pretty at the top spot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the wake of Grand Theft Auto 6's release and the wave of glowing reviews it received, a war is raging in Metacritic's user reviews, with some of the medium's best games of all time caught in the crossfire.

Industry observers note that if you take a look at Metacritics' best games of all time list, you'll see Grand Theft Auto 6 sitting pretty at the top spot. Yet, if you take a gander at some of the others following close behind it, you may notice a sudden increase in very negative reviews from those riding hard for Rockstar's latest release.

Take the user reviews for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which held the top spot for years prior to GTA 6's launch. You can see such pearls of wisdom as: "L Japanese Propaganda. GTA 6 better grafics **** it loser Japanese people," from a user called. Mimm1. Or this gem from danzerthethird: "ass nhbgvfyghjgvfghbjnbhgfycvgjbhguytguyhuytyfgutfgyrc7fytghugytfughtvfygbhjgfycurtyvghbgvfycutryvgcfrgv.".

The same is true for the original Soul Calibur. Its user reviews includes newly delivered pieces of critique like this from user GTABEST2456: "Slop game dethroned by GTA 6, 99 on metacritic N1, now this is third LOOOOOOL, get rekt. I played through and I wish there was less zelda references more niko bellic.".

Even Super Mario Galaxy 2 wasn't safe. Customers have taken to review- bombing this game too, an example being BoroqueTsunami who wrote: "Peak Nintendoslop ️ Jump man gimmick. Y'all thought it was sweet until Rockstar pulled up." All of these reviews, across all these non-GTA 6 games, were written following the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

While it is unclear whether GTA 6 fans shot the first bullet here, or whether anti-GTA 6 Metacritic brigaders are to blame, what is apparent is GTA 6 is itself being hit with a counter-offensive of sorts. "Retaliation for Zelda review bombing," wrote user Lucius26. "I didn't choose this war, but I'll fight it all the same. GTA fans, we were not your enemy. GTA6 just made people mad. You like a bad game, accept that.".

According to recent reports, this is all obviously silly and only helps to make the user review section of Metacritic less helpful for people actually trying to get a gist of what these games are like from members of the public. This also stems from a lack of verification on whether people have actually played these games before writing their takes.

In a recent development, whether events like this will prompt Metacritic to implement some additional quality control remains to be seen, though it has been a continuous problem for a while now and this is hardly the first time review-bombing has been used by some of the more bizarre fans of big-budget releases. In fairness, Metacritic is not the only platform to have suffered from this. Steam, too, has had a history of user review-bombing, with Valve adding features to help curb this over the years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the road to Avengers: Doomsday, the multiverse is a touch too familiar. But back in 2022, our expectations were limitless as the walls broke down between several cinematic universes amid Disney's acquisition of Fox.

So, who better than the Sorcerer Supreme to tap into the magic of that concept alongside a handful of genius what-if castings and a deliciously evil villain in Scarlet Witch?

Sources indicate that but even before cameras began rolling, there was an obvious concern. A movie called Multiverse of Madness has to live up to the promise of its title. The Doctor Strange sequel certainly delivered on that potential from the outset by installing Evil Dead and Spider-Man's Sam Raimi as director. Already, Marvel had a winning hand – and Raimi made it count. After Loki and Spider-Man: No Way Home cracked open the door to alternate worlds inside the MCU, Doctor Strange 2 swept across planets and fired through different realities – ensuring a comic book movie played out, well, actually like a comic book for once. Groundbreaking, I know.

Recent findings suggest that this being Sam Raimi, though, there's a playful mix of horror and heartache alongside the trippy visuals. Scarlet Witch may be the focus, but Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was propelled along by Stephen Strange's reluctance to let Rachel McAdams' Christine Palmer, the love of his life, go for good. This isn't Peter Parker and MJ's will they/won't they romance, but a more mature way for a hero to realize he doesn't always get the girl and hits harder than I expected upon a rewatch.

On top of the emotion, there was a generous helping of fan service, largely thanks to Earth-838's Illuminati.

Patrick Stewart once again taking a seat as Professor Xavier feels especially welcome in the weeks since the actor's passing, while the rest of the group tasked with staving off multiversal threats – Captain Carter, Black Bolt, Lashana Lynch's Captain Marvel, Baron Mordo, and John Krasinski's Mister Fantastic – were a grab bag of fancasting favorites and second chances that harnessed the creative brilliance of the multiverse.

Welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

According to recent reports, elsewhere, Scarlet Witch is a strange case – no pun intended – in Multiverse of Madness. Elizabeth Olsen openly admitted to being the only real authority to the movie's creatives about how her character arc went in WandaVision (she finished filming the Disney Plus series just days prior to production beginning on the Doctor Strange sequel). While the hunt for her children across realities made sense in theory, it becomes too huge of a leap for someone who was at least coming to terms with her losses by the end of her time in Westview.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It all culminated in a death that was dramatically heavy, but left her family – and the audience – with too many loose ends and a gnawing sense of loss across Agatha All Along and VisionQuest.

Sources indicate that but dead doesn't always mean dead in comic book movies. In the grand scheme of the MCU, Scarlet Witch's demise was keenly felt, even if we collectively knew it wasn't necessarily permanent.

The decision to retcon her inevitable revival into a way to entrench Doctor Doom's position as the next Significant Bad of the multiverse was an inspired one.

In a recent development, enter Doctor Doom. In the VisionQuest post-credits scene, Robert Downey Jr.'s masked supervillain arrives at the ruins of the Darkhold Castle in Mount Wundagore to resurrect Wanda and claim her powers for his own twisted quest to save the multiverse. In one fell swoop, it makes the end of Multiverse of Madness and what comes next in Avengers: Doomsday all the more interesting – not least because we know just how powerful Scarlet Witch is in the MCU. Doom already has Hulk and Scarlet Witch on his side, with Spider-Man possibly on his radar too. Turning some of Marvel's most iconic heroes against the Avengers (via fair means or foul) would open up far more narrative possibilities than an all-against-Doom battle.

Avengers: Doomsday sounds like the darkest Marvel movie yet, which is why it needs a pinch of Deadpool & Wolverine.

Industry observers note that then, there are the incursions. Admittedly, Doctor Strange and the Multiverse of Madness' post-credits scene isn't all that memorable. Not yet, anyway. Charlize Theron's Clea showing up to tell Doctor Strange he needs to clean up some cosmic mess, though, at least allows Marvel Studios to retroactively act like incursions were present throughout the past half-decade's stories. The literal collision of universes is a substantial deal, with the Russos even describing it as a "profound" devastating event. Much like Scarlet Witch's arc and return, it's a neat piece of tidying-up for something that otherwise rang hollow.

Recent findings suggest that as the joke goes, Kevin Feige can look you dead in the eye and tell you something was always the plan, despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary. That has never been more obvious – and better implemented – than in the connective tissue between Multiverse of Madness and Avengers: Doomsday.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18 in the US and 16 in the UK.

Sources indicate that look ahead with our list of upcoming Marvel movies and check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order ahead of your next rewatch. See you next week as we revisit Thunderbolts.
