📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now unveiled that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a upcoming, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:.

According to recent reports, "We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!".

The message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That stated, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's presently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro.
  • Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X.
  • In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's presently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro. The game doesn't offer a 60fps performance mode or an option to unlock the frame-rate, but one industrious player has managed to do it anyway on Xbox.

Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game.

In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates.

In a recent development, first, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz.

According to recent reports, before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume.

In a recent development, after the second game rolls out, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user said the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this problem, so they run at their normal speed.

Sources indicate that as much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Legendary BBC football commentator John "Motty" Motson, who died in 2023 at age 77, is being added to EA Sports FC 27 through "a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself." The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.

Industry observers note that motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames, but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series states "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "fresh AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.

"My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred noted. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.".

Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." The BBC report also notes that EA paid the Motson family an undisclosed sum for the right to use John's voice.

Not everyone shares Fred Motson's enthusiasm. While plenty in the EA Sports FC subreddit are excited by the prospect, others refer to it with terms like "shameful," "disrespectful," "gross," and "bloody dark.".

"What a bleak fucking world we live in," redditor forameus2 wrote. "You can't even escape in death.".

"Honestly, it's kind of gross for me," jlo1989 added.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"If anyone from my family uses AI to resurrect me in some perverse way like this, I'll fucking haunt them," niallmul97 wrote.

Peter Caulfield of the Save Our Voices Now campaign against unauthorized voice cloning told the BBC he wouldn't care if Motson had signed a deal with EA allowing it to use his likeness after his death.

"But in life or death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," Caufield said, adding that family members shouldn't "automatically" have the right to grant permission for AI recreations either.

At least one other game studio has taken a very different approach to the subject: Earlier this year, Darkest Dungeon developer Red Hook Studios said it would never use AI to recreate the voice of beloved narrator Wayne June, who died in 2025, despite having explicit permission from June himself to do so.

"I would never, ever erode his incredible and timeless performances by teaching a machine to sound like him," Red Hook co-founder Chris Bourassa stated at the time.

The Japan Actors Union also recently began a push to protect the rights of voice actors with regard to AI, including a proposed ban on using AI to copy a dead actor's voice unless consent had been obtained prior to their death.

It's a bit surprising this crossover hasn't already happened, to be honest, given IO Interactive is the studio behind both of the games, but it's now been confirmed a Hitman and 007 First Light collaboration is happening.

The content is live from today until 24th December 2026, and it takes the form of a upcoming Elusive Target in Hitman. Lenny Kravitz, who is playing Bawma from 007 First Light, is the next celebrity to feature in Hitman, but this time, he's on Agent 47's side.

Bawma has been betrayed by three of his associates, and he's called in the bald assassin to take them down.

Up for elimination are Horace Stockton, Oswald Spoon, and Zui.

The new set of Elusive Targets and the mission hosting them brings with it the likeness and voice of Lenny Kravitz, who you'll hear from throughout the level via Agent 47's earpiece.

"Bawma is such a fun and interesting character to portray, so I was excited to step back into a newly introduced world with him for 007 First Light," stated Kravitz. "Seeing Bawma team up with Agent 47 is something I think fans of both games are going to love.".

The mission will be available until 24th December, but if you own a copy of the game, then you'll retain permanent access to the Arcade version of it. It can also be accessed free of charge for those who don't have Hitman 3, as it's being added to the demo of the game.

Alongside the mission, a roadmap detailing the Season of Bawma teases the following content additions: a fresh Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, a new challenge, a batch of Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop and an IOI Account reward.

Will you team up with Lenny Kravitz to take down his associates? Let us know in the comments below.

It has been revealed that another day, another Steam upgrade! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

Industry observers note that for starters, there's a upcoming Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in.".

According to recent reports, next up in the enhancement is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

There were a few other smaller bits to this enhancement too. You'll find a new section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've got some new data coming out about the UK games market in November 2026 today, and unsurprisingly, it's a market that's been absolutely dominated by the launch of GTA 6 last week.

According to the folks at The Game Business, sales of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S rose by a whopping 75% during GTA 6's launch week, which represents the biggest jump for Xbox hardware since 2024.

The PS5 was close behind at 46%, and console sales were up 38% overall (after a 29% increase the week before).

In terms of UK console sales, PS5 sales rose 46% during the week GTA 6 came out, while Xbox Series S and X sales jumped 75%. It’s the biggest jump for Xbox since 2024. Overall, UK console sales last week were up 38%, which comes on the back of a 29% increase the week prior.

Meanwhile, the controversial "physical" edition of GTA 6 broke numerous records in Europe, serving as the biggest physical launch in Spain's history according to their charts, and selling over 1m physical copies in France in three days.

It was also the biggest physical launch in the UK since FIFA 20 in September 2019, and is the 17th biggest physical launch since records began there in 1995. This is according to data provided by UK data tracker Nielsen IQ.

"GTA 6 is the biggest physical game launch since 2019, reveals UK data tracker Nielsen IQ. It generated £32 million in revenue in just three days.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gaming tech giant Nvidia has decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, despite allegedly saying it wouldn't, and despite a string of extramarital affairs and investigations into alleged bullying, workplace harassment, and humiliation.

Recent findings suggest that "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's Chair Harvey C. Jones announced on behalf of the Nvidia's board today - the same person reported as saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's chief financial officer.".

In the same press release, Huang said he was "honoured" to return to the tech giant "at the beginning of a newly introduced industrial revolution". "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said.

However, the investigation into one of Huang's extramarital affairs - the one with the person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy - will "proceed to conclusion". The company also said it formed a "National Security and Export Control Committee", with independent directors, in relation to this.

It has been revealed that huang resigned on 12th November a few days after his affair with the alleged Chinese spy came to light. Two subsequent affairs - both said to be with Nvidia employees and therefore his subordinates - were unearthed not long after, putting increased pressure on Huang and Nvidia.

Since his departure, Nvidia stock has tanked, and as news of his reinstatement spreads around the world, it has sharply recovered again.

According to recent reports, for publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.

In a recent development, "We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest. "If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers. In terms of the budget, I gave a response [in an interview at] Gamescom; games The Witcher or Cyberpunk 2, although they are not GTA, are not budget-driven developments.".

Recent findings suggest that nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus. "They are ambition-driven developments and money is important, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6." This is obviously kind of a non-answer in one sense, but I think it does point to how GTA 6 is going to create some uncomfortable expectations for many triple-A devs when next to none of them will have Rockstar money to fulfill them.

According to recent reports, in any case, obviously the next massive thing for CD Projekt Red is The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. Still no release date attached to that one, though it's right now expected to release sometime in 2027 next year. The Witcher 4 is then slated for release not long after that in 2028, but in this day and age, I'm sure a delay would be an incredibly safe bet to make.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar just issued a fresh patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few problems players have been reporting since the game launched last Thursday (19th November).

In a recent development, the 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an upgrade on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

There have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

In a recent development, but there's one matter here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

It has been revealed that the beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a latest patch for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

The sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape.".

There are a few fresh subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction.".

Beyond this there's a selection of fresh weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this update as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

Analyst Suggests Console Prices Won't Drop Until At Least 2028

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that we've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too.
  • Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching upcoming consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.
  • According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too. But if you were hoping 2027 would be the year things finally get cheaper, well, according to S&P boffins, it doesn't look likely.

Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching upcoming consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.

According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".

"[2028 is] the earliest point at which launching latest consoles at accessible price points looks prudent,".

In layman's terms, these digits suggest supply might finally begin catching up with demand in 2028, potentially bringing down the cost of PCs and consoles.

DRAM is essentially a console or PC's super-fast short-term memory. Whenever you boot a game, its data is loaded into DRAM so it can be accessed and processed swiftly. The more DRAM you have, the bigger and more ambitious games you can play.

The image above gives us a breakdown of the additional DRAM supply expected from each manufacturer, pointing to 2028 as the earliest point at which prices could start to get smaller.

In a recent development, however, that's relying on a consistent demand from data centres. If it continues to grow, all that additional DRAM could be gobbled up by the AI industry. Likewise, if demand is less popular than predicted, supplies could return quicker.

Recent findings suggest that "If data centre demand grows, then it could swiftly eat into the extra supply...The memory [fabrication facilities] are not expanding with an eye specifically toward the consumer market. They're racking up record revenue and margins on the data centre build-out, so these supply expansions are primarily meant to feed that demand.".

Recent findings suggest that microsoft's next-gen Xbox Helix console is rumoured to be launching in 2028 with a suspected price tag of over $1,000. Barbour weighed in on Microsoft's Xbox Series supply shortages.

"If Microsoft is suffering from supply shortages with the current Series consoles, as it has said a few times over the past year, then they will almost have to wait for the upstream component supply to shore up before they make a substantial push with a fresh console.".

Recent findings suggest that what are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

GTA 6 vault: How to open them during big bank jobs

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a substantial score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.
  • But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.
  • Sources indicate that here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a substantial score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.

But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.

Sources indicate that here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.

Sources indicate that your GTA 6 fence, Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun.

Complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, and in Chapter 4 he'll offer you a tip for $10,000. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.

In a recent development, there are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!

In a recent development, you can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Major Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City International Airport.

Sources indicate that follow the armored car until it parks outside a bank. Watch as one of the drivers gets out and walks into the bank. You can follow him to see where he goes, though bank layouts differ and he may take different routes. He may walk through the front doors, or he may go in a side entrance or a roll-up door in the back.

Once he's all the way inside—not just inside the front doors, but deep into the bank—he'll head to the vault and open it.

You can't open that vault yourself! Only the armored car driver can. That's the trick.

Once the guard is in the back of the bank, begin the robbery. Search for the vault in the back. You may need to use explosives to open the door the guard went through, or you can look for a door you can open with the snap gun. You'll find the vault door open with the armored car driver nearby. Subdue him and grab all the cash off the cart inside the vault.

According to recent reports, there are several safe deposit boxes in the vault you can open for extra loot. Use your focus ability to highlight which boxes you can loot, and shoot them to open them up. You can also blow open all the boxes at once using a grenade or sticky bomb. Grab the loot from each.

According to recent reports, if you really want to clean the place out, there's still all the cash drawers in the front of the bank and a small safe, or multiple safes, somewhere else, usually in an office in the back. You can open these standard safes with safe codes.

The armored car parked outside has loot in it, too. The thing is, it may despawn while you're inside the bank. If you want to loot it, place a sticky explosive on the rear door, which won't let the truck despawn. (Be stealthy: there's another guard still watching the truck). When you leave the bank after the robbery, detonate the bomb and grab the loot.

The best way to enter a bank is through a back door, if the building has one, (using the snap gun to avoid alarms) or a roll-up door. If the guard you're following goes in the back, he may leave the doors unlocked behind him, and you may not even have to unlock any doors at all to reach the vault. Just be prepared to run into multiple security guards and employees you'll need to subdue.

You will want both Jason and Lucia along for any bank vault jobs you pull. There is so much cash and valuables to grab you'll easily fill up four bags, which requires two people to carry. (You can hand loot bags to your partner by interacting with them and choosing the "Hand over bag" prompt). You'll also want one character to work as crowd control while you're looting the bank.

A silenced gun is a good idea: you want to delay setting off alarms for as long as possible, and if bank employees or citizens hear gunshots they may panic and trigger the alarm, or flee from the bank and call the cops.

Sources indicate that in a lot of robberies you can find the security footage and destroy it while the robbery is in progress. Major banks have cloud-based cameras which won't allow you to destroy the footage. Keep a lookout (using focus) for cameras and shoot them out (with silenced pistols) as promptly as you can.

In a recent development, if an alarm goes off during a vault robbery, you'll get an instant four-star wanted level, which means SWAT trucks, roadblocks, and helicopters. Park your car in a good spot outside so you can jump into it easily, and have some idea of where you want to drive to during your escape.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a newly introduced trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

The trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and newly introduced playable faction.

Now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was announced, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

Industry observers note that in its final few seconds, the trailer demonstrates a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was quickly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively upcoming addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Industry observers note that vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

It has been revealed that what this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bucky Barnes actor Sebastian Stan has defended Thunderbolts after its weaker box office performance.

The film grossed $382 million, which, while not an outright disaster, also isn't a stellar return for Marvel.

According to recent reports, "I think it's just when you've had a studio and you've had Marvel, and it's been so many years where they've just been knocking it out of the park, a $350 million global number just suddenly doesn't seem that much. But it's insane how much money that is, you know?" Stan said on the Next Best Picture podcast.

Sources indicate that "So, I don't know, I still felt like for us it felt like a success," he continued. "I know a lot of care went into that and it had more nuance to it in terms of, I guess, than some of the recent ones. I don't know, from my point of view at least. Like, dealing with real complications like mental health and depression and so on. They're just a good group of people.".

Stan will soon return in Avengers: Doomsday, a crossover for the ages that puts the Avengers, Thunderbolts, Fantastic Four, and the X-Men up against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

"We love this film. We've poured a lot into it. We've had seven years to think about it. We've got Robert back, greatest actor in the world," co-director Joe Russo said recently. "I think it is unlike any movie that's been made in the Marvel universe up to this point. It's tonally very different. It's very surprising, and I think the audience is going to be very surprised when they see the movie.".

Doomsday arrives this December 18. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV highlights for everything else that's on the way.

Xbox CSO Responds To Criticism Around Game Branding, Promises To Fix In 2027

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (304 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are declared and Xbox doesn't make a big deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.
  • In other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are declared and Xbox doesn't make a big deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

In other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and latest Fallout games where it felt like they were unveiled without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is unveiled / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

Let's see what happens in the New Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together. However, there was one huge event that didn't include David Schwimmer's character, and there's a specific reason why. While Ross's absence from this particular scene was unfortunate, it did lead to a clever joke and a nod to something the character had become notorious for.

According to recent reports, the end of Season 6 of Friends was a big one. Chandler had done too good a job throwing Monica off the scent of his planned proposal – so much so that it seemed like she was actually considering Richard's proposal of marriage and a family – and was frantic to correct the situation. The big twist came when he came rushing back to the apartment, being made to believe he was too late, only to find Monica waiting for him with a proposal of her own.

Industry observers note that monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them. The only person absent was Ross. No, David Schwimmer and Friends weren't "on a break," he was just busy overseas when the engagement scene was filmed.

As Friends co-creator David Crane pointed out on the DVD commentary, all of David Schwimmer's scenes for the two-part Season 6 finale had to be filmed in the first week because the actor was in England filming Band of Brothers for HBO. Crane spoke about having to film the scene without Schwimmer, saying:.

Recent findings suggest that it was frustrating not having him because you feel as though there's a major event on the show, Monica and Chandler are engaged, and all the friends run in, but not quite all the friends. The moment still works, and it's still moving, but it would have been nice to have him for that, but we were not prepared to film that scene the previous week.

According to recent reports, while all of the drama between Monica and Chandler was going on throughout "The One with the Proposal," Ross was busy breaking up with college student Elizabeth (a cliffhanger involving her revealing she's pregnant was discussed for the season finale, but ultimately scrapped). From what it sounds like, that was all filmed during the first week of production for these final episodes. The grand finale involving Chandler and Monica wasn't filmed until later.

As you'll recall, as the gang is celebrating with a group hug, Phoebe points out that "Ross isn't here!" to which Rachel responds, "Oh, hell, he's done this three times. He knows what it's about!" It's a funny way to acknowledge and then dismiss Ross's absence from his sister and best friend's engagement, while also firing a shot at Ross's "three-divorce guy" reputation. As Crane put it, that was the silver lining to the situation, after debating whether or not to point out the lack of Ross in the scene:.

There was a lot of debate. Do you need to acknowledge the fact that Ross isn't here? Or do you just let it go? And it actually gave us a really good joke.

I'll admit, the absence of a main character due to the actor being involved in another project might bother me under other circumstances, but it's hard to complain here. Band of Brothers is its own kind of epic, after all. Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks' HBO miniseries – based on Stephen Ambrose's non-fiction book about a parachute infantry manufacturer serving in World War II – won several Emmys and has been widely remembered and appreciated in the decades since its release. What's more, Schwimmer's portrayal of Captain Herbert Sobel is easily one of his most memorable roles outside of the hit sitcom.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

The writers made the best of the situation by working in the joke about marriage proposals being old hat for Ross.

Ultimately, Ross did get in on the celebrations for Monica and Chandler, but it doesn't happen until the start of the following season. Ross learns about his sister and Chandler's engagement early in the Season 7 premiere, when he reveals up at the apartment with a bottle of champagne and a candy bar that they requested him to bring.

You can watch Friends and Band of Brothers with an HBO Max subscription.

There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few fresh bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger looks for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original upcoming levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

According to recent reports, variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first indicated up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Recent findings suggest that amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Sources indicate that earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

There's no release date yet for the show, but it's stated to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon.".

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

Recent findings suggest that "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency.

Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings.

On whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche mentioned during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question.".

Blanche also noted that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal.

"A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer said on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, according to sources speaking to Reuters, Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, the latter of which is the company associated with Alice Huang (no relation), the woman with whom Huang admitted to having an affair. (The CEO also reportedly had affairs with Nvidia employees.).

In his return address to Nvidia staff, Huang remarked (via Marisa Kabas) that the company's board opted to bring him back of their own accord, not because of pressure from the Trump administration. That statement is contradicted by Trump himself, who told CNBC that he "convinced" the Nvidia board to bring Huang back.

Trump is an Nvidia investor, and Nvidia donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom project.

Huang is scheduled to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a upcoming Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie.".

"Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch.".

If you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

Industry observers note that the job post is by no means confirmation that a upcoming Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly upcoming game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie demonstrated up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

Recent findings suggest that composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he said at the time.

I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

Astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a substantial space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

As you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various latest vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Plan or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

Sources indicate that and then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

'The Results Are Very, Very Impressive' - Digital Foundry Praises GTA 6 On Xbox One

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.
  • Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.
  • Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

Sources indicate that "Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.".

It has been revealed that performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones.".

Recent findings suggest that from their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

It has been revealed that streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

It has been revealed that latency also looks to be the big winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

"Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.".

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

Of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Industry observers note that have you tried Xbox Cloud streaming GTA VI? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands.
  • As documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools.
  • The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-notable executable file, which was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek.

As documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools. Going by Hendricks's posts, which are based on watching a Leonida stream, much of the recomp's creation seems to have consisted of one or more high school kids typing prompts like "work faster", while spending hundreds or thousands of dollars in usage fees.

The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds.

As reported by PCG, the Leonida Discord server has now been shut down, and the Github repository for the recompilation's code has been nuked. Hendricks has shared an alleged takedown request from a representative of Take-Two Interactive, according to which Github have taken action against 3,007 forks (that is, duplicates for the purposes of making a separate version) from the original Leonida repo. Meanwhile, somebody has set up a leaderboard to chart the progress of several other GTA 6 recomp projects. I'm sure Take-Two's IP enforcement teams appreciate their efforts.

According to recent reports, A few days prior to GTA 6's release on console last week, Rockstar North's former tech director Obbe Vermeij told RPS that the GTA makers would release the PC version sooner than anticipated to avoid losing any cash to generative AI rip-offs. IGN subsequently asked Take-Two's CEO Strauss Zelnick for his thoughts on this. Zelnick replied that the manufacturer are "not in the least cavalier" about the risk, but are confident people would rather play the game as Rockstar intended.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox has given eager fans an patch on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a upcoming blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)".

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.".

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox stated he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible.".

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

It has been revealed that "Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way".

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence.".

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two released together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

According to recent reports, we don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that "Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023.
  • Despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review.
  • In a recent development, but now that's changing too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023. While ostensibly about battling dinosaurs, "you first go through an interdimensional time portal controlled by a rogue AI, and then you compete in a Hunger Games-style contest against alternate universe versions of yourself for the AI's amusement. That's where the dinosaur killing comes in.".

Despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review. And it didn't catch on: A year later, Capcom announced the end of new updates for the game, although the game remained fully playable.

In a recent development, but now that's changing too. Capcom announced today that Exoprimal services will be terminated on September 29, 2027, at which point the game will become unplayable. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years," Capcom wrote, "and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

The sale of seasonal "survival passes," which have been rotating through Exoprimal's four seasons since the end of updates in 2024, has been halted, while the game itself along with all DLC and "other products"—there's quite a lot of it—will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. After that, the game will tick on—and Capcom hopes you will continue to enjoy it—until the end of the road in September.

It sucks to see games fail, especially when they have the potential to grow into something good, and it's even worse when they don't just tank but become completely unplayable because of their reliance on external servers that no longer exist. This is one of the primary drivers behind efforts like Stop Killing Games: Wherever possible, the end of a game's service should not signal the end of the game.

It's a principle I broadly support, but in the case of Exoprimal it's fair to say that not too many people will be impacted by the shutdown: SteamDB indicates that the peak concurrent player count over the past 24 hours was just 23. Exoprimal is also available on consoles so there are more players in total than just that, but how many more? I don't know, but I'd guess not too many.

He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from newly introduced game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

  • Sources indicate that facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year.
  • Industry observers note that "This latest system isn't really new," Newman wrote.
  • Similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year. That rough start has it in need of a redemption arc, which the Rust devs are hoping will be powered by going free-to-play and making changes like the revamp of sandbox mode they've just rolled out.

Industry observers note that "This latest system isn't really new," Newman wrote. "It's the exact same system that Garry's Mod uses. I hold my hands up here, I thought that spawning from the cloud was better...but I was wrong. There definitely is something a lot nicer about installing a substantial model pack and then having everything right there. I'm sorry it took me so long to come around to realising this.".

Similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well". "I'm excited by all the possibilities of it," he continued. "Obviously there aren't a ton of addons right now but what we do have is showing a LOT of potential, and that's only going to grow. I've been going through improving things that feel outdated or stupid. I'm resisting bending it all too far, I want it to stay kind of familiar for everyone, but I think we can improve a few things in our upcoming engine.".

A number of old school sandbox props, such as chunks of robotics, wheels, gears, and hunks of steel girder are on their way back, while Facepunch are finally ready to add in water. "It has waves," Newman wrote of the latter. "The physics objects get tossed around in the waves. You can go underwater, and swim, and there's caustics and fog and particles and post process effects and stuff." Also, NPCs now "live directly in the engine" making it easier to set up a fight club.

A simplified menu and a whole bunch of performance and dev-focused tweaks round out this update, so go through the full notes if you're keen to read about the likes of workshop mounts and VRAM fragmentation.

According to recent reports, as of writing, S&box is still yet to go free-to-play, a change Newman and co previously said is coming "towards the end of the year". If it can nail recapturing the classic GMod magic with updates that players actually want, I think it stands a chance of a comeback. However, as its lifespan thus far has proven, it's harder to rely on high quality user-made games within a game than ever before in an age when people can just resort to using generative AI for an ever-increasing number of things.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought.
  • According to recent reports, "The exe is out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

According to recent reports, "The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects.".

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

According to recent reports, in just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, stated in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

In a recent development, as for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token.".

Sources indicate that rockstar has not unveiled a PC version of GTA 6, but the manufacturer has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report remarked GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

These latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been breaking records all over the place, so it doesn't come as much of a surprise to learn that its performance at physical retail has been mighty impressive.

As reported by The Game Business, based on data from UK tracker Nielsen IQ, GTA 6 has recorded the country's largest physical launch since 2019's FIFA 20. Turns out only the nation's love of football can compete.

GTA 6's physical sales generated £32 million in revenue in its first three days. Apparently, it's the 17th biggest physical launch in the UK ever.

That might not sound particularly grand, but if you consider how much the physical market has shrunk over the last few years, it's actually pretty remarkable.

All this has transpired despite the game's physical copies coming with a download code rather than a disc, something that caused some anguish among collectors and enthusiasts.

I think it maybe proves that people will still show up for a physical product, even in a world where discs are on their way out.

PlayStation looks to discontinue making discs for its platform starting in 2028, but it's possible we'll still see physical rolls out for major games — just with a code in the box instead of a Blu-ray.

Anyway, GTA 6 has been selling well on all fronts, surprise surprise. Did you pick up the physical version of the game? Tell us in the comments section below.

"More than just war and peace": Total War: Medieval 3's diplomacy system will build on Three Kingdoms' backstabbing, with rulers who aren't just focused on you

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise.
  • Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.
  • In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise. Diplomacy! The soul of any Total War game. They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "newly introduced heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day.

Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.

In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".

In a recent development, as regards "believable agendas", Creative Assemble want the campaign AI to display both a survival instinct and the ability to "pursue its own interests instead of primarily being an antagonist to the player". These agendas will span the game's Politics, Economy, and Families systems, with dynastic considerations affecting behaviour. They want you to be able to read another ruler's intent by tracking back through their past actions. They want weaker factions to sue for peace or seek sensible alliances, rather than "stubbornly being entrenched in a war it is bound to lose". Aww, but I love it when Scotland does that.

The game will aim for a balance of long-term thinking and opportunism, with AI leaders pouncing on short-term prospects even as they keep the whole in mind. And then there are inconvenient "ripple effects": you might get involved with a neighbouring succession crisis because you don't want to deal with the fallout if, you know, That Guy takes the throne.

Speaking of borders, Creative Assembly also want would-be treaty-makers to think harder about terrain and transportation. "For example: You finally reach a faraway realm with your diplomat, opening diplomatic relations to a realm far beyond your initial sphere of influence," Wojs goes on. "Relations are positive, but meaningless due to the lack of physical proximity. Once that faraway realm has access to a port, a trade route can finally be established. This leads to an exchange in culture and trade, and may finally allow you to recruit foreign units into your service.".

Industry observers note that I have to say, I do find a lot of this language either broadly familiar from previous Twars, or too general to reveal much. There is, however, a closing in-game anecdote from principal designer Thomas Schut that digs into the detail. Schut gives the example of you sending a diplomat to negotiate a 10 year non-aggression pact greased by recognition of another ruler's royal title, in return for their vassalage. Sending a diplomat allows you to negotiate on the spot, but if you'd rather not spare a diplomat, you can also dispatch sealed letters at the price of not being able to see and respond immediately to the other faction's reaction.

Rulers can make public claims to cities, calling on other rulers to support them. Simply conquering and annexing them will damage your standing in every court. You can also forge claims to cities, if only as insurance against wanting to own them someday. Get enough rulers to back you, and you'll be able to throw around grander pronouncements about what you're divinely entitled to. You are the Emperor of Everything! Coalitions will apparently form and fragment over years, old friends turning on each other as their dark plots come to light.

In a recent development, the joy of Cao Cao puppetry notwithstanding, I don't play Total War for the chance to thrash out cunning pacts with bots. I am here to put my archers behind my spearfolk - and hope the other side's cavalry don't notice the cutthroats I've stationed in the woods. I'm more interested in what I've read about Medieval 3's regional levies system. Still, it does sound like Creative Assembly are serious about giving you things to do besides putting other wannabe kings to the sword.
